After a humiliating defeat by Grimsby Town in their previous League Cup campaign, Manchester United found a different way to exit the competition this time around. The jeers heard at the full-time whistle after throwing away a two-goal lead pointed to more worrying times a year on from Blundell Park.

For the first time in half a century, United lost a game at Old Trafford having led 2-0, highlighting the defensive problems Michael Carrick needs to solve after turning results around last season.

“What the f---ing hell was that?” shouted the home fans, in a chant that may have been aimed at the referee but equally applied to United’s players, who led through Shea Lacey and Mason Mount’s early goals.

Brighton cut through Carrick’s defence several times before staging their comeback with goals from Charalampos Kostoulas, Pascal Gross and Maxim De Cuyper. Carrick and his analysts will rewatch the footage of all three goals in horror at how they conceded.

It has been revealed that erik ten Hag used the domestic cups to taste success while struggling in the Premier League, but one of those opportunities is now lost to Carrick, who must be careful not to spiral from a poor start to the campaign into crisis. “We have a significant game on Sunday that we have to prepare for. We’re out of this competition and we have to go back to winning football matches.

It has been revealed that “It doesn’t feel good at the moment. It doesn’t feel good. We have to go back to winning football matches. We want to win and want to win rapidly. The next game is Sunday. That’s all I’m thinking about right now.”.

Tra infortuni e il caso Rodriguez, il tecnico granata attende risposte dal campo prima della sfida contro la Lazio.

Sources indicate that in vista della sfida tra Torino e Lazio, valida per la 13ª giornata di campionato, l'infermeria porta diversi dubbi in casa granata. Come riportato da Toro News, Abate deve valutare vari acciacchi emersi dopo Napoli e situazioni da chiarire tra difesa e fasce, pur con qualche buona notizia, e le ultime indicazioni sul campionato arriveranno direttamente dalle parole del tecnico prima del match.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

According to recent reports, restano forti dubbi sull'impiego di Rafik Belghali contro la Lazio: il ginocchio destro infiammato (senza lesioni a menisco e legamenti) lo ha costretto al cambio al 40' al Maradona dopo aver stretto i denti al rientro anticipato dalla nazionale, e solo Abate chiarirà se potrà correre senza dolore. Stop più lungo per Ardian Ismajli: uscito nella ripresa a Napoli per una lesione di primo grado agli adduttori della coscia sinistra, salterà almeno tre settimane, a cui si somma l'operazione di osteosintesi alla mano destra per il quarto metacarpo che impone massima cautela.

Sulla sinistra resta in bilico Cristiano Biraghi, fermo a lavorare a parte per un affaticamento muscolare che lo staff valuterà giorno per giorno senza forzare, con convocazione incerta anche per la panchina. Segnali positivi invece da Niccolò Fortini, che ha superato la pubalgia ed è già tornato in panchina a Napoli: sta seguendo un percorso di potenziamento per ritrovare ritmo, e spetterà al tecnico decidere se impiegarlo con la Lazio o attendere ancora.

Il caso di Ricardo Rodriguez non è solo medico: dopo il recupero dall'infortunio pre Monza, ha risposto alla Svizzera giocando durante la sosta, attirando la dura reazione del Torino che lo ha escluso per motivi disciplinari a Napoli (scelta su cui Abate non ha avuto potere decisionale). Fisicamente sembra recuperato, ma resta da capire se verrà reintegrato per la sfida con i biancocelesti.

David Moyes’ record-breaking night as Everton manager could not have been more miserable.

In his 593rd game as Toffees boss, Moyes broke Harry Catterick’s 75-year record for most games in the dugout.

But that was about the only positive he could take away from the Gtech Community Stadium, as high-flying Brentford battered ten-man Everton on an evening to forget for the 63-year-old Scotsman.

Daily Mail Sport's Bobby Manzi was at the Gtech Community Stadium on a torrid night for the Toffees...

The Bees can mix it with substantial boys.

Brentford, having missed out on European football on goal difference last season, are showing all the signs of being there or thereabouts again.

They climbed to sixth, leapfrogging Leeds — who have had far more praise lavished on them this season than Keith Andrews’ reliable side.

Brentford are disciplined with plenty of attacking flair, even with frontman and top goalscorer Igor Thiago suspended.

The Premier League lacks quality this season, but Brentford are consistent, losing just twice.

This well-oiled Andrews machine must take advantage of the floundering elite, with Manchester United, Chelsea and Tottenham all struggling, and finally secure Europe.

‘We set out this season looking to be better than last season, and if that happens, we will be flying to different destinations next season,’ Andrews remarked of their European hopes.’.

Industry observers note that ‘We've got a very competitive squad that strives to get better. If we continue with that mindset, we'll hopefully be in a good place.

Industry observers note that ‘I enjoyed us,’ he added about the performance. ‘I thought we were very good. We played with real bravery, courage and energy.’.

Brentford limited Everton to just three touches in the penalty area in the first half. They grabbed the game by the scruff of the neck and pinned their opponents back.

Jaidon Anthony was superb on the flank, providing two assists. Midfielder Vitaly Janelt capped off a brilliant display with a wonder strike from 25 yards, finding the top corner with his left foot.

It was a surprise to see Kevin Schade benched but this team is so cohesive, with more focus on the unit than any individual stars, that victory was light work for them.

Both of Keane Lewis-Potter’s goals had an element of fortune attached. But teams earn that luck when they manage ten shots in their opponents’ penalty area in just 45 minutes.

Sources indicate that lewis Potter starred at left-back, registering seven shots — the most of any player — and the joint-most touches in the opposition box. He was a menace and integral to every Brentford attack.

James Tarkowski endured a depressing return to his former club when he was shown the first Premier League red card of his career.

It will split opinion, but in this day and age it is a clear red card. Although the Everton defender won the ball, his studs connected with Yehor Yarmolyuk’s shin on follow-through.

Sources indicate that the speed and intensity of the tackle endangered his opponent. He had to go.

Sources indicate that referee Craig Pawson brandished a yellow, but a quick trip to the monitor saw it upgraded. Tarkowski ran down the tunnel before Pawson could even get the red card out of his pocket.

The home support enjoyed it, having taunted their former player throughout the first half.

To compound Everton’s misery, the first game of Tarkowski three-match ban is next weekend’s Merseyside derby.

‘But after I saw it again, Tarky's boot is a bit higher than I'd like, so I can understand why the decision went against us.

In a recent development, ‘We didn’t play well. Brentford did and credit to them. A bit unfortunate with the goals, it made it look even worse than it was.’.

Everton were unbeaten in four games at Brentford before this and their defeat came in the form of the sublime and the ridiculous.

In a recent development, the first goal was all about Anthony undoing Everton on the left before Lewis-Potter was given far too much space to get his shot away. The deflection was unfortunate, but the defending was poor to begin with.

Industry observers note that tarkowski blocked an initial effort from Lewis-Potter for the second goal but the ball fell straight back to him, and Jake O’Brien helped his second attempt past Jordan Pickford. Once again, Everton should have done better and cleared the initial free-kick.

Chiariello: “Migliore in campo Allegri, tre spanne sopra tutti”

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (572 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Iamnaples

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, umberto Chiariello, giornalista, ha commentato a Canale 21 il pari del Napoli con il Manchester City in Champions League: “Migliore in campo Allegri, tre spanne sopra tutti.
  • I Am Naples Testata Giornalistica - aut.

According to recent reports, umberto Chiariello, giornalista, ha commentato a Canale 21 il pari del Napoli con il Manchester City in Champions League: “Migliore in campo Allegri, tre spanne sopra tutti. Perché ci ha sorpreso tutti, con uno schieramento che nessuno aveva immaginato, prima mettendo in campo Lang, che era dato in panchina, ma soprattutto spostando Spinazzola a destra e giocando con il 4-3-3, con De Bruyne mezzala, che è il suo ruolo, numero 8, sacrificando Anguissa e facendolo entrare nel momento opportuno, quando la pressione era insostenibile e De Bruyne non ne aveva proprio più. Stasera due non mi hanno soddisfatto, De Bruyne e Milinkovic-Savic Perché De Bruyne ha avuto due palle al 57° e al 67°, me le sono appuntate, dove è solo a palla, Hojlund gli detta la profondità, uno come lui lo deve mandare in porta alla squadra, non per fare il lavoro di sacrificio. A me stasera De Bruyne non è del tutto soddisfatto perché quello che ci doveva dare, la qualità, non ce l’ha data. Si è sacrificato tanto, ma non ci serve questo da De Bruyne. Milinkovic sul primo gol va giù e deve rimanere in piedi, quella palla se rimane in piedi la prende, ma sul secondo si schiaccia proprio sul palo. Lui sbaglia la traslazione, si schiaccia sul palo, non può stare lì, deve lasciare un po’ di palo e coprire la porta. Il tiratore deve trovare lo specchio coperto, lui sbaglia la bisettrice, totalmente la traslazione, va sul palo e non è la prima volta che noto questo suo atteggiamento. Quel gol ce l’ha sulla coscienza. Ed è un peccato perché avevo appena finito di elogiarlo per la partita precedente. Ha mostrato personalità in uscita, qualche parata brutta ma efficace, ce n’è stata una nel primo tempo che mi ha fatto tremare, che l’ha presa in maniera raffazzonata, però aveva retto. Ma alla fine io penso che sia successo esattamente come 15 anni fa. L’ottimo De Sanctis, che a Napoli fece molto bene, in quella partita purtroppo non fu impeccabile e il Napoli, che meritava di vincerla con Mazzarri, la pareggiò 2-2. La stessa cosa capita 15 anni dopo, ancora il portiere non impeccabile. Gilmour è stato sicuramente tra i migliori in campo. Io premio Politano per il sacrificio e per la palla che dà a Spinazzola sulla destra, che è favolosa, ma Gilmour sicuramente ha fatto una grande partita, la migliore. Vorrei citare un giocatore nel suo ruolo, finalmente, centrale a due di difesa: Beukema ha dimostrato che non è un bidone e se Beukema prende fiducia, almeno con questo investimento possiamo pensare che torni qualcosa. Così come Lang forse è l’esterno che stavamo cercando e che, dandogli fiducia, ce l’abbiamo in casa”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Dopo la parentesi biancoceleste e l’esperienza a Maiorca, il centravanti conta sei reti in 12 gare di campionato.

Sources indicate that vedat Muriqi segna ancora e il Fenerbahçe vince di nuovo. Il centravanti kosovaro ha realizzato 10 gol e servito due assist in 22 partite. A 32 anni è tornato protagonista nel club di Istanbul, riconquistando l’affetto dei tifosi.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Il club lo ha inseguito a lungo in estate. Muriqi era già stato un idolo dei tifosi durante la sua prima esperienza in Turchia e, dopo aver giocato anche a Maiorca, è tornato a vestire la maglia del Fenerbahçe.

Il suo rendimento accompagna questa seconda esperienza a Istanbul: i 10 gol e i due assist nelle 22 gare disputate raccontano il momento dell’attaccante, soprannominato Pirata.

In campionato Muriqi ha segnato sei gol in 12 presenze, partendo titolare cinque volte. In Champions League ha disputato cinque gare, quattro dal primo minuto, e realizzato due reti arrivate in momenti importanti.

È stato decisivo nelle ultime due sfide contro Liverpool e Shakhtar. Aveva già segnato nei preliminari contro il Lione. Le sue prestazioni hanno contribuito a ridurre lo spazio di Romelu Lukaku nelle gerarchie offensive della squadra, soprattutto nelle notti europee.

#154330. Floyd Samba’s Man City debut double has father Chris dancing

📅 17 Sep 2026 • ⏱️ 20m • 📚 Deep Dive (4072 w)

Floyd Samba’s Man City debut double has father Chris dancing

📅 17 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 20 min read (4072 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~20 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.
  • This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.
  • But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.

This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.

But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.

Floyd Samba scored two fine goals and had a hand in another on a dream debut that had his beaming dad up off his seat and thrusting his arms in the air as if ready to party.

If the Samba surname feels familiar, that is because Floyd’s father Christopher played more than 200 games for Blackburn Rovers, Queens Park Rangers and Aston Villa.

In fact, it was very much a family affair as Floyd’s brothers Tyrone and Emerson, who are also in City’s academy and hoping one day to tread a similar path, joined in the jubilant celebrations alongside their mother, a visibly emotional Theresa.

This particular evening belonged to Floyd, though. Deployed as a lone striker by Enzo Maresca, you would not have known he ordinarily plays as a midfielder such was the confidence and composure the 17-year-old oozed.

Norwich could not live with him or City for that matter as Maresca’s impressive start as manager since replacing Pep Guardiola continued apace.

It has been revealed that this must have been an incredibly satisfying moment for Samba Sr. He came through incredible hardship – at one stage as a teenager he was rough-sleeping – to forge an impressive career totalling more than 450 games for club and country.

So to be in a position to now have three sons in City’s academy and one produce a debut like this will fill him with enormous pride. Floyd was later seen enjoying a warm embrace with his dad in the crowd, moments after being congratulated by Tyrone, a year his senior, and 12-year-old Emerson, who plays for City’s Under-13s.

“I knew there would be an opportunity to get some minutes for the first time with the first team – to get a debut like that is mind blowing,” Samba stated. “I couldn’t believe it myself, but that’s just the beginning, I’ve got a big career ahead of me. It was a great debut.”.

Floyd caught the eye with a fine free-kick in City’s 2-1 FA Youth Cup final victory over Manchester United last season and now he has goals for the senior side to his name. Pretty stunning they were, too.

The first was a superbly steered header past two Norwich bodies on the line from Allan’s cross and the second a lovely, nonchalantly curled finish low into the far corner.

It has been revealed that what a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn.

Chris Samba has deliberately kept a low profile, keen to let his sons get on with their own careers free of distractions, but there was no chance he was going to be able to suppress his emotions in that instant. And nor should he. It was some moment for the boy and his family.

In a recent development, as impressed as Maresca was by the goals, it will have been other elements of Samba’s game that also caught the eye. He did extremely well to hold off the attentions of Norwich’s centre-backs when receiving a pass from Ayyoub Bouaddi and then returning the ball to the Moroccan who released Rayan Cherki through to score City’s second. His movement was also sharp, at one point taking a difficult pass sweetly in an adjusted strike, only for Norwich’s Bruno Alves to come across to make a timely intervention before Samba could get his shot off.

"Was there any doubt?"Ayyoub Bouaddi with his first assist for Man City as he sets up Rayan Cherki to make it 2-0 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0gfxp5GDXy.

“It was satisfying not just for the two goals but for the entire performance,” Maresca remarked. “He didn’t play many games as a nine but he was good. He’s young, full of energy, strong, he can finish.”.

Allan, a £34m summer signing from Palmeiras, will have been just as pleased with his contribution. Maresca’s fluid formation initially resembled a 3-1-5-1 with Allan effectively operating as a right wing-back but he stuck doggedly to the task before eventually getting the moment to showcase his quality, first with his cross for Samba and later with a neat solo run and finish.

Driving inside Sam Field and then cutting back inside the Norwich man before curling an inch perfect finish into the bottom corner – all of it done with his left foot – it was quite the introduction.

Allan on his debut! 🇧🇷Magic from the Brazilian to make it 3-0 to Man City 💥 pic.twitter.com/nw6lNqh1yL.

Hugo Viana, City’s director of football, has said supporters will need to be patient with Allan and that it may take the 22-year-old time to adjust to English football but this first outing will do his confidence plenty of good.

“It was vital for him to play 90 minutes and to see a little bit the English competition that is a bit different from South America so overall was good,” Maresca said.

In a recent development, cherki was the only survivor from the team that started Sunday’s victory over Manchester United but it all felt pretty seamless from City. Bouaddi, the £85m signing from Lille, was poised and graceful in midfield alongside the impressive Mateo Kovacic and Geronimo Rulli could not have asked for a much quieter debut in goal.

FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1.

Nico O’Reilly looked like he had barely broken a sweat despite Norwich’s players routinely being unable to keep up with him. Norwich themselves made nine changes but the gulf in class was enormous and testament to City’s strength in depth.

The game also gave Maresca the opportunity to give run outs to two more academy graduates who played in that Youth Cup final triumph, Kaden Braithwaite and Ryan McAidoo and the latter got his own name on the scoresheet to make it 5-0.

In a recent development, all told there were seven City academy graduates on the pitch, two of them playing for Norwich. This was certainly a night to remember for the club’s youth production line.

With the dominant performance, Man City have earned themselves the privilege of hosting Brighton in the next round, who will no doubt prove a much stiffer challenge than Norwich. They become the sixth all-Premier League tie in the next round, with only Fleetwood, Bradford and Peterborough remaining from outside the top flight:.

Possession: Man City 66% vs 34% Norwich.

Touches inside opposition box: 30 vs 4.

Erling Haaland left out of the squad, watching from the stands, would have enjoyed that performance from Floyd Samba. Here is his second goal for you to enjoy on his debut night:.

FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1.

Five unanswered goals and a home-grown hero emerges for Manchester City!

Great through ball from O’Reilly, which Lewis lets run past him for the dummy. McAidoo runs on to it on the right of the box and first-time fires it low into the far corner.

It has been a perfect night for Manchester City’s academy.

Well we look like we’re heading for a matching scoreline to the previous edition of the fixture. That pesky shot on target is still eluding Norwich, whereas Samba is still out there looking for his hat-trick.

Two minutes of time to be added – who will get there first?

O’Reilly sends a high, looping ball to the back post from the left side, where McAidoo rushes to meet it but can’t get over it under pressure.

Final change for Norwich, as Kvistgaarden who has not had much service tonight, comes off for Schwartau.

Bouaddi sends a looping ball across the field to McAidoo, which he picks up on the edge of the box, but he is unable to get the ball under control to take his shot and it is cleared away as far as another City shirt.

The corner comes in to the centre of the box but is headed out by a City shirt.

It’s all slightly too little too late for Norwich.

They get another corner as Musaba tries to send a cross into the box from the right and it is blocked out.

A free-kick for Norwich now as O’Reilly commits the foul 35 yards out. It goes in towards McConville at the back post, but Ait-Nouri heads it out for a Norwich corner.

According to recent reports, mo Touré strays just offside on the edge of the box, as Musaba sends a lovely little ball over to find him on the turn and the forward slots it past Rulli. Celebrations don’t quite begin before the flag goes up but that is a shame for the visitors.

Norwich have managed to get more of a grip in this half, despite conceding two more goals, but they are still without a shot on goal as we approach the final 15 minutes.

Another round of changes for both sides.

Man City take off scorer of their third goal Allan to bring on Braithwaite.

Norwich replace Ben Slimane and Bruno Alves with Touré and McConville.

It has been revealed that samba again at the heart of the action, laying off the ball to McAidoo on the right for the winger to run into the box. His shot towards the far post is saved low by Grimshaw who spills it almost into the path of Lewis, but Norwich survive.

Lewis makes a run down the right-hand side and crosses into Samba on the edge of the box. He lays off to McAidoo, but his shot goes sailing over the bar.

A surprise to no one, it is chucking it down in Manchester.

Massive cheers from the away end as Norwich get their first corner of the evening. It is lofted high and long to the back post, where it is headed away by Bouaddi. It bounces out to Musaba, who has just come on, and he strikes it from the top of the box on the half-volley.

His shot cuts through a crowd in the box and has Rulli diving to his left, but it goes wide of the post. What an introduction that would have been!

Well all the stories from this match will be all about young Floyd Samba. Feel free to leave your best punny Samba/dance-related headlines in the comments section.

For Man City as you would expect it is all about game management from here on out.

Some more changes to report for Norwich as well, as Crnac is replaced by Musaba.

Wright is able to run in to space towards the edge of the box, but as has been their story all evening, his pass out to the wing is just not where it needs to be and their effort just breaks down.

In a recent development, what a way to score a second! A night to remember for Floyd Samba!

It has been revealed that norwich try and play out from the back but far too sloppy and Ait-Nouri picks up the ball on the left of the box. He has plenty of time to tee up Samba inside the box at the left corner, who finds himself with plenty of space to curl his shot into the far corner, beating the diving Grimshaw.

We may be seeing plenty more of him this season.

Norwich looking for their way back into the game, as the ball comes down the left, fizzed in low and flashes past Rulli, trying to claim it. It deflects off a crowd of bodies and spins up, but Fisher can’t connect and it spins away harmlessly wide of the goal.

It is definitely Norwich’s best chance of the game and Fisher will be upset he hasn’t made more of that.

According to recent reports, and Allan makes it three! Minutes after the restart, the Brazilian makes his own mark on his debut.

Maresca switched him onto the left side to escape Yongwa, and he picks up the ball outside the box and makes the run inside. He runs circles around Field and slots the ball home into the far bottom corner.

Recent findings suggest that some changes from both sides at half-time. McAidoo comes on for Cherki, though O’Reilly is the one to move up into midfield to fill the gap.

Norwich take off Diallo for Maghoma.

45 minutes left for the visitors to create something special!

It has been revealed that what a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn.

Manchester City will be the ones to host Brighton in the next round – giving the visitors the opportunity to pull off a remarkable feat of knocking out both Manchester sides should they win.

Enjoy the highlights from last night as they came from behind to dispatch Man Utd:.

Possession: Man City 72% vs 28% Norwich.

Touches inside opposition box: 15 vs 1.

Sources indicate that and without much ado at the end of the half, we have reached the break. City put themselves in control with two quick-fire goals and it looks a tall task for Norwich to find their way back into the match.

Credit where it is due, Yongwa has been very good for Norwich. He has stood fast, made some very good challenges and stopped Allan getting much of a look-in on the right.

Sources indicate that as we approach half-time, the stats tell a sorry story. Norwich have had just 28% possession and created a single shot, none on target.

As City come again, Norwich have pulled every man back to try and keep the situation salvageable before the break.

Samba was in again there, making a run into the box with a ball from Cherki, wrestling with Bruno Alves as he goes. The defender does enough to throw him off and Grimshaw is able to come out and snatch the ball.

Man City are looking to close this out now, and they look threatening every time they break.

Ait-Nouri is the latest to try his luck, making a run into the box from the left, but his shot is blocked.

Industry observers note that A few minutes to remember here for Floyd Samba. First he steers home a very well taken header to give City the lead and then he plays a crucial role in the second, holding the ball up well before laying it off to Bouaddi to release Cherki to score. That’s how to make an impression on your debut.

According to recent reports, and the floodgates have opened. Two goals in two minutes for the defending champions.

According to recent reports, samba finds Bouaddi in midfield, who takes it forward and feeds Cherki running to his left. He gets himself one-on-one and slots cool as you like into the bottom left corner.

City are in control all of a sudden and Norwich will be devastated.

As soon as I say that, Floyd Samba finds a way through.

Recent findings suggest that he has looked the brightest for City, and O’Reilly sends a cross over the box from the left, drawing Grimshaw away from position. The ball is pinged back in by Allan and the youngster stoops to meet it, heading in to the bottom corner.

Norwich have been very disciplined in defence so far. Yongwa has been closing down Allan on the wing very well.

Cherki is starting to get some momentum – but is swarmed by yellow shirts as he picks up the ball on the edge of the area.

Another loose ball from City in midfield and Norwich pick it up again. The ball to set the front line free is equally as loose from the visitors though and it breaks down once again.

Sources indicate that samba is looking lively, racing to get on a ball in front of Darling just on the edge of the box. Darling recovers to send it out for a corner, which becomes a free kick after Ait-Nouri wrestles his man to the ground at the back post as City are taking.

Wright sends a long ball across the field, looking for a man on the right side but Rulli is alert to it and comes to claim at the edge of the box.

Kovacic shows some promise with a strong run on the ball down the centre of the field, taking the ball all the way to the edge of the box, where he collides with a defender, and the ball spins away for Norwich to clear out.

This is better from City, who have looked like they’re lacking drive so far.

Yongwa again probing down the left side. It takes two to dispossess him and Man City manage to get the throw in, but approaching 20 minutes Norwich will be happy with this.

According to recent reports, kovacic loses the ball in midfield and Norwich surge forward. The move breaks down as Wright’s pass to Diallo on the wing is just behind him and he can’t take it forward into the box.

Sources indicate that spent the first 10 minutes trying to work out City’s system and settled on a 3-1-5-1, with Bouaddi operating as a nominal third centre-back, but it seems to have changed again now with O’Reilly dropping to left back and Bouaddi stepping into midfield. No doubt the metamorphosis will continue.

This Man City team have never played all together and it is clear that they’re still settling in here, figuring out how they’re going to press here.

Kovacic in the captain’s armband is tying it all together in midfield.

According to recent reports, khusanov threads a lovely ball to Samba who flicks it into the path of Lewis, who takes it and makes a run into the box. He creates space and sends a right-footed shot over the bar – but Man City are building.

According to recent reports, norwich make a move forward, with Yongwa bringing the ball down the left side but his cross into the box is blocked by Allan sliding in. The Brazilian is then fouled again as Yongwa tries to reclaim the ball and Man City get back in possession.

It’s actually three Samba brothers at City. The youngest, Emerson, is also in the academy.

Early foul on Allan gets Man City a free kick and they have started as everyone expected they would – in plenty of possession.

They look for the early goal as O’Reilly feeds him in the from the left side, but the shot is blocked.

We have kicked off in Manchester!

With just over 10 minutes until kick-off here are the teams for tonight’s fixture:.

Man City XI: Rulli; O’Reilly, Vitor Reis, Khusanov, Lewis; Kovacic (c), Bouaddi; Ait-Nouri, Cherki, Allan; Samba.

Subs: Anderson, Braithwaite, Donnarumma, Fernández, Guéhi, McAidoo, Ndiaye, Matheus Nunes, Semenyo.

Norwich City XI: Grimshaw; Yongwa, Bruno Alves, Darling (c), Fisher; Field, Wright; Diallo, Ben Slimane, Crnac; Kvistgaarden.

Subs: Chrisene, Mattsson, Kovacevic, Maghoma, McConville, Musaba, Schwartau, Stacey, Touré.

"It's part of the decision that I took when I decided to join this club"Enzo Maresca responds to the doubts surrounding him filling Pep Guardiola's shoes 👇 pic.twitter.com/o6eUjQUOnU.

David 🆚 Goliath 🤝🎥 https://t.co/5YXw2tQvfX pic.twitter.com/fTp9zD0xiX.

As Abdukodir Khusanov makes his fourth start of the season, Hugo Viana, Man City director of football, has been speaking about the young Uzbek. The 22-year-old signed a fresh five-year contract with City in July, and Viana has affirmed that he “will be one of the best centre-backs in the world”.

"Abdukodir Khusanov will be one of the best centre-backs in the world" - Hugo Viana 🇺🇿🌏Full interview 🔗 https://t.co/dk3Qi8DF8D pic.twitter.com/hHdVdX5HSF.

It’s nine changes for Norwich from the squad that lost 4-3 to Middlesbrough on the weekend.

Norwich goalkeeper Daniel Grimshaw came through the ranks at Manchester City, joining as a teenager, so this will be a special night for the 28-year-old.

In a recent development, speaking of Phil Foden, the winger will not be making an appearance tonight, as he is serving his three-match suspension following his sending off in the Manchester derby. The England international lashed out at Bruno Fernandes after the United captain had fouled him, resulting in a red card for violent conduct.

As well as this fixture, he will also be missing City’s game against Sunderland and the trip to Anfield to face Liverpool the following weekend.

We broke down the incident as it happened on Sunday and you can get the full story here.

Heavy squad rotation (10 changes in total for Maresca) has handed debuts for Gero Rulli in goal, as well as Allan and Floyd Samba in the outfield.

According to recent reports, 17-year-old Samba is the latest from City’s academy to be making his debut in the senior squad, following in the footsteps of Phil Foden, Rico Lewis, Nico O’Reilly and many more. A versatile midfielder, he has totalled 24 appearances across six competitions (incl Premier League 2) and scored 17 and assisted six goals in those matches.

Keep your eyes on young midfielder Floyd Samba, who has been handed his Manchester City debut tonight against Norwich by manager Enzo Maresca. Floyd is the 17 year old son of former Blackburn Rovers defender Christopher Samba.

His older brother Tyrone, 18, also plays for City. The siblings played in City’s FA Youth Cup final win over Manchester United last season, with Floyd scoring the first in a 2-1 win.

City fans will also be keen to see how Allan Elias gets on on his first start, having arrived from Palmeiras for £34m. Geronimo Rulli also debuts in goal.

Checking in 🚌🚶‍♂️ pic.twitter.com/xWYGyaH7TY.

Manchester City or Norwich vs Brighton.

Ⓒ Darling with the armband🧤 Grimshaw in goal⚡️ Ante on the rightYour Yellows for this evening ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/znOGtvyJyk.

Good evening and welcome to another night of Carabao Cup coverage! It is the final fixture of round three (I promise) as Manchester City host Norwich.

In a recent development, these two sides have not met since 2022, when Norwich were still in the top flight and were beaten 4-0 by City. Looking at their previous meetings, the odds are definitely stacked in favour of Enzo Maresca’s side, who have scored 14 unanswered goals in their last three meetings with Norwich, while the Championship side have not scored any.

City will be looking to make it six straight wins across all competitions tonight, having started perfectly in the Premier League with four wins from four, and comfortably seeing off Porto in their Champions League opener.

They were the talk of the weekend with their deeply controversial 1-0 win over rivals Manchester United as – having gone down to 10 men after Phil Foden was sent off – their winning goal was allowed to stand despite Enzo Fernández being clearly in an offside position that impacted United’s keeper and backline.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy.

City are defending their title in this competition – beating Arsenal last year in the final – but like all Premier League teams playing in European competitions, have only entered the tournament this year in the third round.

Sources indicate that philippe Clement’s side beat MK Dons 4-1 in the first round, and followed that up with a 2-1 win over Cardiff City in the second to reach the Etihad tonight. The fourth-round draw has already been done, and it has been decided that the winner of this match will face Brighton.

But we have at least 90 minutes of the third round left before that, so without further ado, we’ll get underway and bring you team updates shortly!

  • "Il Como è per distacco la sorpresa del torneo.
  • "L’Inter è a un punto dall’ottavo posto, dipenderà dagli scontri diretti contro Dortmund e Liverpool.

Dalle colonne del Corriere dello Sport, Massimiliano Gallo fa il punto sul cammino delle italiane in Champions League dopo cinque turni. "L’ultimo turno di Champions ci ha consegnato le nostre squadre protagoniste. Con due vittorie e due pareggi. Non solo. Negli ultimi tre turni, le italiane hanno vinto otto partite su dodici (grazie soprattutto a Como e Inter che hanno fatto en plein). Solo due le sconfitte: il Napoli a Porto e la Roma che ha subito la rimonta in casa del Manchester United. Il quadro non è così fosco come invece ci ostiniamo a descriverlo".

"Il Como è per distacco la sorpresa del torneo. L’Inter ci ha ormai abituati bene. Le vittorie nerazzurre contro squadre sulla carta abbordabili, vengono date per acquisite. Lo Stoccarda ne è un esempio. E poi i due pareggi che valgono più del punto in classifica. La Roma di Gasperini è andata a giocarsela alla pari in casa del Psg, senza Malen né Dybala titolari. Sì anche i francesi avevano tanti assenti ma sono pur sempre i vincitori delle ultime due Champions".

"L’Inter è a un punto dall’ottavo posto, dipenderà dagli scontri diretti contro Dortmund e Liverpool. Roma e Napoli sono fuori dalle prime 24 ma di poco. Entrambe hanno un calendario sulla carta positivo, poi ovviamente le partite bisogna vincerle.   • He is, though, ruled out of Bayern’s game this weekend.

Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany has confirmed that they will be without Michael Olise for their Bundesliga game against Hamburg on Saturday.

The Frenchman was injured in last weekend’s 1-1 draw against Cologne and subsequently missed Bayern’s UEFA Champions League defeat against Lille on Wednesday night. Olise, who left the Allianz Arena on crutches after a challenge from Cologne’s Tom Krauß at the edge of the box, has been wearing a VACOped brace to help with the recovery process after suffering bruising on his left foot.

He is, though, ruled out of Bayern’s game this weekend. “Olise won’t be there,” Kompany mentioned at Friday’s press conference. While Serge Gnabry, Ismael Saibari and Harry Kane are all sidelined, Luis Díaz returned against Lille – in a game where Lennart Karl led the attack – after sustaining a thigh injury during their 2-2 draw against Arsenal in October.

An attacking trio of Konrad Laimer, Tom Bischof and Nathaniel Brown started on Wednesday, but Kompany remained tight-lipped on who will start against HSV. “We have to make the most of the hand we’ve been dealt,” he added. “So everything remains open, but our expectations and standards remain exactly the same.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that milutin Osmajic è tra le sorprese del primo spaccato di Serie A 2026/2027. L’attaccante montenegrino classe 1999 ha già segnato sei gol in 11 partite di campionato e punta alla doppia cifra.

Alla vigilia di Inter-Genoa, Osmajic ha rilasciato un’intervista ai microfoni de’ La Gazzetta dello Sport.

Lei sa di essere già nella storia del Genoa, visto che una partenza come la sua, con sei gol in undici partite, l’avevano fatta solo Milito e Piatek con la maglia rossoblù?

“Di questo non posso che essere contento. Un momento… magico, certo. Sto molto bene, ma soprattutto sono molto felice di vedere il mio club andare bene e vincere. Ora, però, è necessario andare avanti così. Voglio continuare a lavorare sodo per il bene del team, non certo perché il mio primo interesse sia di aumentare i gol segnati”.

A Genova frequenta lo stesso ristorante dove anche il Principe Milito era di casa.

“Ci sono andato quattro o cinque volte, a me piace moltissimo la carne, mi dà grande energia, la consumo tutti i giorni, ma qui da voi ho imparato anche ad apprezzare la pasta con il pesto”.

Affrontate l’Inter domani, che ha giocato mercoledì in Champions e presenta qualche problema in difesa. Può essere un vantaggio per voi?

"Parliamo di un top club, non credo che possa avere difficoltà in tal senso, perché il livello è comunque altissimo. Dobbiamo solo provare a fare la migliore partita contro di loro, rimanendo concentrati in tutte le zone del campo, perché ogni possibile errore si paga a caro prezzo contro avversari del genere. Semmai, bisognerà trovare le possibili soluzioni per cercare di essere comunque pericolosi".

Se lo aspettava così il campionato italiano?

"Innanzitutto è molto differente il modo di giocare fra la Championship e la Serie A. In Inghilterra c’è un calcio più fisico ed aggressivo, a volte devi stare attento a salvare le tue gambe. Qui è un’altra cosa: grandi giocatori, ottimi difensori, per me è la miglior lega possibile a livello calcistico".

  • Radja Nainggolan has claimed his former team-mate Romelu Lukaku is planning a 'bombshell' statement on Belgian football following his shock retirement from the national team.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 04:37 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 04:38 EST, 24 November 2026.

Radja Nainggolan has claimed his former team-mate Romelu Lukaku is planning a 'bombshell' statement on Belgian football following his shock retirement from the national team.

Lukaku, 33, unexpectedly announced his retirement from international football following Belgium's Nations League matches against Turkey and Italy earlier this month.

Belgium's all-time record goalscorer had been left on the bench against Italy, while he had not been in the squad three days earlier for the match against Turkey.

Lukaku's shock announcement caught Belgian media by surprise, while his former international team-mate Nainggolan has claimed more news will follow from the star.

Nainggolan, who won 30 caps for the national team between 2009 and 2018, revealed on the Ongefilterd Voetbal podcast he had a one-hour phone call with Lukaku following his decision.

The former Inter Milan and Roma midfielder stated that Lukaku told him: 'You are only allowed to say that a bombshell is about to explode.'.

Romelu Lukaku announced his shock retirement from international football earlier this month.

Former team-mate Radja Nainggolan claims Lukaku is planning a 'bombshell' statement for Belgian football following a one hour phone call with the star. Source: Ongefilterd Voetbal.

'So something is still coming,' Nainggolan noted.

'What? I don't know. There were some internal problems between him and a certain person. But I'm not going to say much about that.

It has been revealed that 'Romelu will bring that up himself. He was a bit bitter, though. He was disappointed, frustrated.

'We will hear from him soon what will happen.

'About the real problems that were at play, he will be able to explain that better than I.'.

Lukaku's retirement had marked a stunning reversal of his plans, with the former Chelsea and Manchester United forward having vowed in January that the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament with the Belgium national team.

Describing his international career as a 'great ride', Lukaku had confirmed his international retirement on social media.

According to recent reports, '16 years old', his Instagram statement began. 'For 16 years, I gave everything for the national team. I experienced every possible emotion. I played with fantastic teammates for whom I will always be grateful.

Lukaku vowed in January that the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament.

The Belgian forward has fallen down the pecking order and spent a lot of time on the bench.

In a recent development, 'I want to thank them all. I also want to thank all the coaches for pushing me and giving me the confidence to help the team. It was a great ride, and I enjoyed every moment.

'To the Belgian fans, thank you for the support you have given our team. I am proud to have represented my country at four World Cups and three European Championships. I will never forget those moments. I am at peace with my decision to stop here. It was amazing, it was a joy. I am grateful. Thank you.'.

The Belgian veteran accompanied his post with a gallery of photographs from his storied international career, from his debut against Croatia under Dick Advocaat in 2010 to his final chapter wearing the armband.

Lukaku has captained Belgium on a handful of occasions since 2020, alongside the likes of Kevin De Bruyne and Youri Tielemans.

The 33-year-old forward, who became one of the hottest properties in world football after breaking onto the scene at Chelsea, has been a regular fixture in the international set-up for almost two decades.

Spearheading Belgium's golden generation, which included star-studded talents such as De Bruyne, Thibaut Courtois and Eden Hazard, Lukaku chalked up an impressive 135 caps for the international team.

He also retired as Belgium's all-time top scorer on 94 goals, just six shy of a century.

After suffering multiple injury setbacks, he featured at the 2026 World Cup under Rudi Garcia and continued to play a crucial role, scoring three times as a substitute to guide Belgium to the quarter-finals where they were ultimately stopped by eventual champions Spain.

Since Mark van Bommel's appointment in August, following Garcia's departure at the end of his contract, Lukaku has slipped further down the pecking order, with Charles De Ketelaere preferred to lead the line.

During Belgium's resounding 4-1 victory over Italy on Sunday, Lukaku warmed the bench as an unused substitute – and wasn't even in the squad to face Turkey three days before.

Lukaku, pictured with Kevin De Bruyne, was an unused substitute as Belgium beat Italy 4-1.

While Belgium were winning in the second half against the Italians, Lukaku was seen warming up on the sidelines in the hope of featuring for one last time, but unfortunately was not given the opportunity.

VTM NIEUWS anchor Maarten Breckx claimed De Bruyne looked 'concerned' while speaking to Lukaku on the bench, suggesting the former Man City star was unhappy to see his team-mate overlooked.

According to recent reports, 'When it became clear that he wouldn't be allowed to come on, De Bruyne was talking to him. You could see the concern in his eyes,' he noted.

Recent findings suggest that 'You could tell, especially from Romelu's attitude, that he was dissatisfied and displeased. He had probably counted on getting some minutes...'.

With only Jan Vertonghen and Axel Witsel registering more international caps than Lukaku over their careers, boasting 157 and 140 appearances respectively, Belgium are expected to give the 33-year-old forward a send-off he deserves in the near future.

Witsel, who also called time on his Belgium career this year, was one of the team-mates to celebrate Lukaku's retirement on Instagram.

According to recent reports, 'Thanks for everything, legend. Thank you, what a journey we've had together,' he wrote.

Christian Ilzer’s substitutes supplied two of the three goals as the Kraichgauer recovered from a disappointing first half to secure an important European victory against their head coach’s former club.

According to recent reports, hoffenheim entered the dressing room trailing 1-0 after Oumar Diakité’s 43rd-minute opener, with sections of the home crowd expressing their displeasure at the halftime whistle. The hosts nevertheless emerged with renewed energy and eventually turned the match around. Speaking to journalists in the mixed zone afterward, Austrian international Alexander Prass insisted that Hoffenheim’s response had not surprised him.

It has been revealed that “No it doesn’t surprise me,” Prass remarked in the mixed zone when questioned about the comeback. “Because we’re just a really awesome crew. We’re capable of banding together even after a total shit first half, or a not so good first half. Sorry. We can up the energy. Every individual can help us mutually bring what was lacking in the first half. We did everything better in the second half.”.

It has been revealed that ilzer’s decision to introduce Patrick Wimmer, Andrej Kramaric, and Bambasé Conté shortly after the hour mark proved particularly influential. Adam Hlozek equalized in the 72nd minute before Conté completed the turnaround eight minutes later, finishing off a Tim Lemperle cross. Substitute Max Moerstedt sealed the 3-1 victory with his first touch in the 90th minute. Wimmer initiated the attack by winning possession, with Kramaric subsequently setting up the young German striker.

Conté, himself one of the decisive substitutes, agreed when asked about the quality of Hoffenheim’s options from the bench.

“Yeah you could say that,” Conté responded in the mixed zone. “We made it difficult for ourselves in the first half. From the restart onwards we produced a very positive energy with the substitutions and we turned the game around.”.

In a recent development, hoffenheim have already benefited from influential substitute appearances this season. As GGFN examined following the club’s 3-0 Bundesliga victory over Bayer Leverkusen, Kramaric also transformed that encounter after entering in the second half, contributing a goal and an assist.

Industry observers note that despite Thursday’s successful turnaround, team captain Oliver Baumann was less inclined to celebrate the performance unreservedly. Speaking to RTL after the match, the goalkeeper criticized Hoffenheim’s first-half approach and stressed that the team must learn to sustain its improved football over 70 or 80 minutes rather than relying on one good half.

Baumann acknowledged that Hoffenheim remain in a developmental phase. The German international nevertheless welcomed the response after halftime, which helped lift Ilzer’s side to 15th place in the Europa League standings.

Thursday’s comeback thus highlighted both the shortcomings Hoffenheim must address and the considerable resources Ilzer has at his disposal. With the likes of Wimmer, Kramaric, Conté, and Moerstedt capable of influencing matches from the bench, the TSG trainer certainly has options when his starting XI struggles to find its rhythm.

#154316. ANALYSIS | This is why Werder Bremen is No.1 in northern Germany

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (990 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Getfootballnewsgermany ↗ Open Full Page

ANALYSIS | This is why Werder Bremen is No.1 in northern Germany

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (990 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Getfootballnewsgermany

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Werder Bremen is the best team in northern Germany.
  • Bremen did more than just win that game; they demonstrated their quality this season and their ability to maximise the potential of their players to become a highly efficient team.
  • This is the glitch: The underlying numbers, in this case expected goals (xG), indicate that the game was actually very close – not as one-sided as the result suggests.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Werder Bremen is the best team in northern Germany. At least that is what was evident from last weekend’s Nordderby, when they successfully beat Hamburg 4–0 at the Weserstadion.

Bremen did more than just win that game; they demonstrated their quality this season and their ability to maximise the potential of their players to become a highly efficient team.

This is the glitch: The underlying numbers, in this case expected goals (xG), indicate that the game was actually very close – not as one-sided as the result suggests. HSV even had 1.54 compared to Bremen’s 1.52 in front of xG, per Opta.

So, being able to win by a four-goal margin despite losing on xG shows just how effective Bremen are as a team. Get German Football News’ Bergas investigates why….

Sources indicate that yes, HSV has more numbers in front of xG. However, if we look at the xG data itself, 1.03 of HSV’s 1.54 came after they fell behind in the 55th minute. In this situation, the state of the game changed, with HSV adopting a more proactive approach with the ball.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, between minutes 1 and 54, when the score was still 0–0, HSV only achieved an xG of 0.5 (Bremen had 0.84). This is why xG is not the best metric with which to measure HSV’s performance in this game, because the state of the game forced them to create more chances in order to catch up, resulting in lots of shots. In fact, however, they weren’t really dangerous enough to challenge or harm Bremen.

It has been revealed that looking at other metrics such as key passes, HSV weren’t superior either during the even time when the score was still 0–0. In that period, they made four key passes compared to Bremen’s eight. HSV found it much harder to create shots than the home team. Even in the first half, when Bremen were underperforming in parts, HSV didn’t look particularly threatening.

Bremen flexible defensive structure made HSV toothless.

One of the reasons for that is Bremen’s flexibility in their approach to HSV when defending. In the first half, they often used a man-to-man approach (which was more aggressive), which successfully forced HSV to use long balls to progress the ball to the final third, particularly on their left side.

According to recent reports, in this long-ball scenario, Bremen also had the advantage when it came to closing down HSV attacks. The problem for Bremen arose when HSV successfully won the second ball, creating a situation in which Amos Pieper had to defend one-on-one against the opponent.

According to recent reports, pieper struggled in the early stages of the game against HSV’s pacey attackers and received a yellow card in the first half, but played safely for the rest of the game and successfully avoided another red card. This was also thanks to Bremen’s improved defensive structure in the second half. They were not as aggressive as before, but rather kept their double six close to their defensive line. With this defensive structure, HSV were unable to find the free space in front of Bremen’s defensive line that they had exploited in the first half.

Even if HSV were able to progress, Bremen’s man-to-man marking prevented them from being exploited by HSV’s overload, which they usually created through asymmetrical or free movement by their players. With every player having their own marker, that situation was difficult to create.

Directness and quality help Bremen win the game.

It has been revealed that one noticeable development from Werder Bremen this season is their flexibility with the ball. Bremen can be a team that dominates possession, but they can also be very dangerous when they need to play directly. This Nordderby is a perfect example of that.

Recent findings suggest that in the minute before their second goal, Bremen only made two passes. Before the fourth goal? Only three. They can score with short sequences because they are very effective. The Bremen players really know how to make direct passes forward and progressive runs to enter the final third as swiftly as possible. They don’t like to slow things down unnecessarily.

This behaviour is exemplified by players such as Justin Njinmah, Marco Grüll, Eren Dinkçi, Mitchell Weiser and Niclas Füllkrug, who excel in direct situations. Füllkrug is special because he knows many ways to score a goal, which has made Bremen more effective this season.

Bremen fans will be hoping that this form is sustainable for the rest of the season. While they have been flexible in terms of their attacking style and have been able to be efficient thanks to the quality of their players, at some point this season they may need a consistent pattern of attacks to help them create substantial chances.

It is clear from this game that HSV need their attackers to show more initiative in the final third. Of all the starters, only Albert Grønbæk consistently tries to create chances in the final third. He made some dribbles to try to break Bremen’s defensive structure and attempted some passes. However, one player is not enough.

Fabio Vieira came on in the second half, but it was too late to help HSV elevate their game. This was made worse by the fact that their top scorer, Miro Muheim, was injured early in the first half. Without their top creators and scorers, HSV practically didn’t have any much ideas in the game.

This problem is not newly introduced. Spectacular goals from outside the box in previous games may have obscured this. However, to survive from game to game, HSV needs more than that. They need a consistent and sustainable strategy in the final third to help them create chances, as well as more initiative from their players to take risks and do more than just shoot from outside the box.

GGFN | Bergas – reporting from the Weserstadion.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • SC Freiburg captain Christian Günter has called for harsher punishment for players who deliberately interfere with the penalty spot following a controversial incident during Thursday evening’s 2-1 Conference League victory over FC Twente.
  • In a recent development, four players subsequently received yellow cards, but Vennegoor of Hesselink escaped a booking.
  • According to recent reports, “I would go so far as to say, as a referee, that he deserves a straight red card,” Günter – as quoted by Kicker – remarked.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SC Freiburg captain Christian Günter has called for harsher punishment for players who deliberately interfere with the penalty spot following a controversial incident during Thursday evening’s 2-1 Conference League victory over FC Twente. Freiburg were awarded a late penalty after substitute Derry Scherhant drew a foul from Bart van Rooij in the 89th minute. Before Matthias Ginter could take the spot kick, Twente striker Lucas Vennegoor of Hesselink attempted to tear up the penalty spot with his spikes, provoking a confrontation involving several players from both sides.

In a recent development, four players subsequently received yellow cards, but Vennegoor of Hesselink escaped a booking. Speaking after the match, Günter condemned the Dutch striker’s actions as “extreme unsporting behaviour” and suggested that such incidents warrant a straight red card. The Freiburg captain argued that football’s lawmakers should consider introducing stricter disciplinary provisions to prevent similar incidents.

According to recent reports, “I would go so far as to say, as a referee, that he deserves a straight red card,” Günter – as quoted by Kicker – remarked. “Do that once, and nobody will go near the penalty spot again.”.

It has been revealed that the incident was not an isolated case of players attempting to interfere with penalty takers. During France’s 1-0 World Cup victory over Paraguay in July, defender Gustavo Velázquez attempted to damage the penalty spot before Kylian Mbappé converted the decisive spot kick.

Sources indicate that A similar controversy arose in September when Mainz midfielder Nadiem Amiri dragged his studs across the penalty spot before Kevin Diks attempted a penalty for Borussia Mönchengladbach. Diks subsequently struck the post in a match Mainz won 4-3. Amiri escaped punishment, prompting former German international Dietmar Hamann to demand a suspension for the midfielder.

According to recent reports, under IFAB Law 12, making unauthorized markings on the pitch is a cautionable offence. Deliberately damaging the penalty spot does not, however, automatically warrant a dismissal. Günter’s proposed rule change would therefore introduce considerably harsher punishment for conduct that has already caused controversy at both international and Bundesliga level.

Scherhant, who won the penalty, appeared less interested in pursuing the controversy after the final whistle.

“Yeah, the opponent tried to sabotage the penalty spot and after that there was some hustle and bustle,” Scherhant remarked in the mixed zone afterwards. “That it gets to that point, that’s naturally not so cool, but I don’t think we need to keep talking about it. We got the points in a game that was difficult for us.”.

The ensuing penalty nevertheless produced further drama. Ginter struck the right post with his attempt but reacted swiftly enough to avoid touching the rebound. Scherhant kept the move alive, Yannik Engelhardt subsequently attempted a backheel, and Niklas Beste eventually converted from close range.

Industry observers note that günter praised Ginter’s awareness in avoiding an illegal second touch and considered Freiburg’s eventual winner a fitting outcome after the preceding controversy. The dramatic conclusion enabled Freiburg to extend their winning streak to six competitive matches and maintain their remarkable run of 14 consecutive European home victories, a streak that began under Christian Streich with a 5-0 Europa League victory over Serbian outfit TSC Bačka Topola on November 9, 2023.

Enzo Maresca, allenatore del Manchester City, ha rilasciato alcune dichiarazioni in conferenza stampa dopo il pareggio in Champions League contro il Napoli.:  “Noi cerchiamo sempre di vincere, ma se non puoi vincere è importante non perdere. Prendiamo il punto, ne abbiamo 10 in classifica e in fin dei conti è un buon risultato per andare avanti. Ricordo un loro calcio d’angolo e i due gol, in questo momento gli avversari sono cinici davanti alla porta. C’è poco da fare, accettiamo il punto e andiamo avanti. L’impatto sui giocatori? In questo momento va un po’ così, le prime dieci partite siamo stati sempre noi a sbloccare, mentre ora sono gli avversari a farlo. Non credo che abbia un impatto sulla fiducia dei calciatori, devi correre un po’ di più se sei in svantaggio, ma abbiamo lottato fino alla fine e serve alzare l’asticella. Non dobbiamo subire questi gol, basta vedere le statistiche a nostro favore. C’è uno squilibrio tra le occasioni create e i gol segnati. Anche Cherki ha detto che mancava energia? Siamo stati molto aggressivi. I due terzini in posizione centrale? Abbiamo iniziato con Bouaddi e Enzo in mezzo per vedere se potevamo trovare equilibrio, poi Nico e Matheus Nunes hanno fatto bene, è un’altra opzione per noi. Volevamo fare qualche cambio ed essere più fisici in mezzo al campo per contrastarli. La qualità del gol di Cherki? Ottimo, sono contento per lui. Ha fatto bene, sappiamo che sa giocare meglio centralmente, ma sta facendo bene. Ci aspettavamo un Napoli col blocco basso, era difficile trovare soluzioni, ma dovevamo evitare di concedere i gol concessi, erano evitabili. I cori a Donnarumma? Non ci ho fatto caso, ero concentrato sulla partita. Era difficile attaccare il Napoli, erano in undici sulla linea dell’area. Potevamo fare meglio nelle chance avute e cercare di evitare le due occasioni concesse. Hanno avuto quelle e il corner di Beukema, c’è rammarico per non aver vinto, ma se non puoi farlo è importante anche non perdere. Non vinciamo da tre partite, ma i meriti del Napoli sono importanti: si è difeso bene e ha concretizzato due occasioni. Noi potevamo fare meglio, il Napoli ha avuto i suoi meriti e ha fatto una buona gara”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Thomas Tuchel faces a fight to regain the full trust of his England players, despite claiming that “99.9 per cent” of supporters do not talk about the semi-final defeat by Argentina.
  • Telegraph Sport reported that players were shocked and disappointed by Tuchel’s approach to the final 30 minutes of the World Cup semi-final.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thomas Tuchel faces a fight to regain the full trust of his England players, despite claiming that “99.9 per cent” of supporters do not talk about the semi-final defeat by Argentina.

Telegraph Sport reported that players were shocked and disappointed by Tuchel’s approach to the final 30 minutes of the World Cup semi-final.

It can now be revealed that doubts linger among England players over Tuchel’s ability to get the best out of his squad and ultimately lead them to glory in the next European Championship.

There is also some lasting unhappiness over Tuchel’s perceived unwillingness to take ultimate responsibility for England’s World Cup exit and his claim that ball possession was not in “the DNA” of the nation’s players.

Tuchel has spoken of fostering a “brotherhood” within the England squad, but a source told Telegraph Sport: “He still has work to do to get all the players fully behind him again. What happened at the World Cup and some of his comments caused some damage that has not just disappeared.”.

Secondo quanto riportato da Il Messaggero, Lotito e Fabiani conoscono la cifra necessaria per rimuovere lo stop, al di là del giudizio della Commissione di controllo. Recent findings suggest that nel 1972/73 la prima sconfitta arrivò contro il Milan, per 3-1, in una gara dell’undicesimo turno recuperata dopo la quattordicesima giornata. La serie positiva raggiunse così tredici partite, ma non si trattò di dodici giornate iniziali completate senza perdere.

Il confronto richiama tre stagioni e altrettanti piazzamenti: lo scudetto nel 1973/74, il secondo posto nel 2022/23 e il terzo nel 1972/73.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SC Freiburg head coach Julian Schuster has praised his squad’s extraordinary team spirit following Thursday evening’s dramatic 2-1 Conference League victory over FC Twente. The Breisgauer secured their sixth consecutive competitive victory thanks to a stoppage-time winner from Niklas Beste, with Schuster emphasizing the importance of a united dressing room in navigating a demanding schedule.

The Freiburg trainer made six changes to the starting XI that defeated Elversberg 1-0 in the Bundesliga last weekend.Cyriaque Irié rewarded Schuster’s faith by scoring the opener in the 11th minute, but Twente remained the more threatening side for much of the first half and eventually equalized through a Younes Taha free kick in the 62nd. Freiburg nevertheless found another way to win. Substitute Derry Scherhant earned a penalty in the 89th minute, and fellow replacement Beste eventually converted the loose ball after Matthias Ginter’s spot kick struck the post.

Speaking to a group of assembled journalists after the post-match press conference, Schuster drew attention to the collective celebrations following Beste’s dramatic winner. The 41-year-old suggested that the team’s togetherness gives him the confidence to rotate extensively without compromising Freiburg’s competitiveness.

It has been revealed that “That scene in which the team celebrated together is emblematic of this group,” Schuster told the journalists. “That lends us the strength to rotate the squad with full confidence. One sees this with various clubs that have to deal with extreme pressure during this phase [of the season]. There’s also players who have international obligations. The pressure is extreme.

It has been revealed that “One really can’t leave anyone out,” Schuster continued. “We have this depth and there’s always little things that leave one needing to switch it up. Then it’s nice when players are ready to serve on a regular basis and not to get caught up in the competition of who makes the team sheet. That’s extremely crucial and I’m very pleased with the lads who started today and were able to make a contribution to the win.”.

Schuster’s observations build on his earlier comments concerning Freiburg’s exceptional dressing-room culture. In October, the SC trainer emphasized the importance of protecting the club’s special atmosphere and ensuring that difficult personnel decisions do not undermine the collective.

According to recent reports, the same philosophy has also been emphasized by Freiburg’s players. Veteran midfielder Maximilian Eggestein recently discussed the importance of sacrificing individual ambitions for the team, while Germany internationals Philipp Treu and Derry Scherhant credited Freiburg’s supportive club culture when reflecting on their own development.

Goalkeeper Mio Backhaus offered a vivid account of the hectic closing stages, during which Ginter’s missed penalty eventually led to Beste’s winning goal.

Sources indicate that “Plenty of chaos,” Backhaus responded when asked about the penalty scene by Baden FM in the mixed zone afterwards. “For [Matthias] Ginter it was also a difficult situation to [take a penalty] four minutes into injury time. And then there was all this turmoil. It was pure ecstasy that Nikki [Beste] pulled that off after all the commotion.”.

Recent findings suggest that “The fact that there were so many of us involved, so many boots on the ground, that helped us re-orient ourselves as a cohesive unit,” Backhaus continued. “The fact that Derry [Scherhant] came on to draw the penalty and Nikki converted [both of them off the bench] also wasn’t a coincidence.”.

Industry observers note that beste had already made an crucial contribution to Freiburg’s previous victory, setting up Igor Matanovic’s winner against Elversberg. The Croatian striker emphasized his instinctive understanding with his teammate after that match, highlighting the familiarity that has developed between Freiburg’s attacking players and the special chemistry emerging within Schuster’s squad.

Club captain Christian Günter similarly regarded the celebrations after Beste’s winning goal as a reflection of the team’s identity.

It has been revealed that “This scene describes our season up to this point effectively,” Günter answered when asked about the celebratory scenes by Kicker’s Carsten Schröter-Lorenz in the mixed zone afterwards. “From solidarity to the fact that everyone wishes everyone else all the best. That the team stands above everything else and that we never give up. And that’s something we’ll have to embody until the very last minute of the very last matchday.”.

“Irrespective of what the situation is, we must remain positive, supportive of each other and stick together,” Günter continued. “One can see that we have the quality and have proven that we can get through games that aren’t exactly pretty and require a lot of fight. We’ve got to preserve that and then we’ll get good things and a good season.”.

Günter’s assessment closely resembles Matanovic’s recent observations about Freiburg’s growing ability to grind out difficult victories. Speaking after the narrow triumph over Elversberg, the striker explained how Freiburg have developed the resilience necessary to prevail in matches that might previously have ended in frustrating draws.

Industry observers note that thursday’s encounter with Twente offered another example. Much like the Elversberg fixture, Freiburg struggled against an opponent that enjoyed lengthy spells of superiority but nevertheless managed to claim all three points.

Industry observers note that the victory extended Freiburg’s winning streak to six competitive matches and marked their 14th consecutive European home victory. The latter run began under former trainer Christian Streich in November 2023 and has continued under Schuster.

With Schuster able to trust both his starters and substitutes, Freiburg’s collective mentality continues to provide a foundation for their success across three competitions.

Former Bundesliga striker Wout Weghorst has expressed his admiration for SC Freiburg’s remarkable development in recent years. The 34-year-old Dutch international, who previously represented VfL Wolfsburg and TSG Hoffenheim, returned to Germany with FC Twente for Thursday evening’s Conference League encounter at the Europa-Park Stadion.

Despite watching his side concede a dramatic stoppage-time winner in a 2-1 defeat, Weghorst was full of praise for the Bundesliga club’s progress.

According to recent reports, “Respect, just simply respect,” Weghorst noted when asked about Freiburg’s scintillating form by Kicker’s Carsten Schröter-Lorenz in the mixed zone afterwards. “I spoke of respect before the game as well. When I was here [in Germany] playing for Wolfsburg and then later at Hoffenheim they were more of a mid-table team. One has beheld a simply amazing development in the last years. Praise to them for that. They’re on a good track.”.

Sources indicate that weghorst became familiar with Freiburg during his four seasons at Wolfsburg between 2018 and 2022 and his subsequent loan spell at Hoffenheim during the 2023/24 campaign. The Schwarzwaldverein were already establishing themselves as regular contenders for European qualification during that period, but their continued progress has since carried them to even greater heights.

Freiburg reached their first European final last season, eventually losing to Aston Villa in the Europa League showpiece in Istanbul. The club nevertheless secured another season of European football and entered the current campaign with a revamped squad.

As Get German Football News examined extensively in our 2026/27 Freiburg tactical preview, the club’s ability to navigate significant departures, reinvest intelligently, and maintain tactical continuity has remained central to its success.

Freiburg’s current European campaign has offered further evidence of that progress. Following November’s hard-fought Conference League victory over Trabzonspor, Schuster’s men have now extended their remarkable home-winning streak in European competition to 14 matches.

Thursday’s contest against Twente was hardly straightforward. The Dutch visitors enjoyed the better of the opening half despite conceding an early goal to Cyriaque Irié. Younes Taha’s superb second-half free kick eventually brought Twente level before substitute Niklas Beste struck in stoppage time to secure Freiburg’s sixth consecutive competitive victory.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 05:07 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 05:13 EST, 24 November 2026.

Premier League clubs are bracing themselves for a newly introduced raid of their talent from Saudi Arabia, as the mega-money league considers relaxing spending rules.

Teams in the Saudi Pro League (SPL) are currently only allowed eight foreign players in their 25-man squads but are discussing increasing that number to 14 or even higher.

If the move is approved, it is likely to trigger a flood of cash in the market similar to the massive £765million spree in 2023 that saw the likes of Cristiano Ronaldo, Karim Benzema and N'Golo Kante sign for Public Investment Fund (PIF) teams.

In that 2023 window, almost half of the transfer fees received by Premier League clubs came from the SPL.

In total, 94 players were signed by Pro League clubs and the January transfer window could now follow a similar pattern.

The Saudi spending reached such astronomic levels that it eclipsed every other league in Europe aside from the Premier League.

Cristiano Ronaldo (right) and Angelo, pictured in action for Al Nassr, are among the foreign stars already plying their trade in Saudi Arabia and more will be on their way.

The supposed reason for the proposed rule change is to elevate the standard of existing Saudi players at home by raising the overall level of talent ahead of the country hosting the World Cup in 2034.

But critics argue that the fresh rules would only force Saudi players out of their domestic league in place of high-profile foreign recruits.

While Premier League clubs are often reluctant to allow talent to leave in January midway through the season, the fees on offer from Saudi can be eye-watering and hard to turn down.

Aston Villa sold Jhon Duran and later Ollie Watkins for a combined £115million to the SPL.

Fulham accepted £50m for Aleksandar Mitrovic, while Wolves banked £47m for Ruben Neves and Liverpool were able to recoup almost £50m for Darwin Nunez.

West Ham were able to cash in on Crysencio Summerville after relegation last term when Al Hilal bought him for £60m.

It has been revealed that would Man United consider offers for Bruno Fernandes as his contract winds down? Or will they keep the club captain to help battle relegation?

Suddenly every Premier League club recruitment department will be reassessing their squads and be keeping a close eye on the rule developments in Saudi.

Ollie Watkins moved from Aston Villa to Al Hilal and the Premier League side have recouped huge fees from the SPL in the  past.

Ivan Toney (second from left) and his Al Ahli team-mates celebrate a goal against Al Nassr.

The SPL's decision on whether to allow the increase of foreign players will be clarified before the winter window opens.

The PIF are winding down their investment in golf through LIV having invested more than £3.7billion since 2021 but their operation in football shows no sign of slowing down.

Players weighing up a move to Saudi will perhaps have a more difficult decision than in 2023 over relocating, with conflict still affecting the country.

The Asian Cup was postponed earlier in November following a missile attack from Yemen-based Houthi rebels on Riyadh airport that killed 13 people and injured more than 300.

Security fears and geo-political uncertainty could make footballers think twice before accepting the lucrative contracts on offer in January and beyond.

Dopo il pari del Napoli per 2-2 contro il Manchester, Giovane ha parlato così in mixed zone:.

“Noi sapevamo che era una partita difficile oggi, il Manchester City è una delle migliori squadre del mondo, quindi il mister ha parlato con tutti noi per entrare con la testa giusta e fare una buona prestazione. È un peccato che abbiamo pareggiato, però è un punto importante per perseguire i nostri obiettivi. Penso che noi abbiamo fatto una buona gara, una buona prestazione. Adesso dobbiamo pensare avanti perché domenica c’è un’altra partita in Serie A. Adesso è già finita e dobbiamo pensare avanti. Qualunque sia il modulo tattico con cui giochiamo, sappiamo quello che dobbiamo fare. Ovviamente si cambia qualcosa quando si cambia modulo, ma penso che anche l’ultima vittoria ci abbia aiutato a prendere fiducia per affrontare oggi questa partita. Giocare qui è difficilissimo perché il Manchester City è una squadra forte. Sappiamo che adesso stanno attraversando un momento difficile, ma non smettono di essere il Manchester City e anche noi non smettiamo di essere il Napoli, quindi è questo. La risposta è quella di sempre, che noi abbiamo quella voglia, quella fame, quella grinta di vincere, è questo. Speriamo che domenica possiamo vincere. Sì, può essere, perché se vinciamo e conquistiamo tre punti così cambia tutto, però anche un punto in una partita come quella di questa sera è importante. La Champions è una competizione difficile, ma adesso dobbiamo pensare avanti e perseguire i nostri obiettivi”.
