The 20-year-old Cologne attacker has spoken enthusiastically about his understanding with the English youngster following their successful attacking combination in last weekend’s 1-1 Bundesliga draw against Bayern Munich.

In a recent development, moore, 19, scored his first Bundesliga goal in the 12th minute at the Allianz Arena, rounding Bayern goalkeeper Jonas Urbig after receiving a return pass from El Mala. The well-worked goal provided a welcome breakthrough for the Englishman following a difficult start to his loan spell in Germany.

As Get German Football News reported following the Bayern encounter, Moore expressed relief at finally opening his Bundesliga account and discussed the growing understanding between himself and El Mala.

Sources indicate that the partnership has been a topic of considerable interest ever since Moore arrived from Tottenham in August. Cologne head coach René Wagner spoke of his enthusiasm for the attacking combination back in September, emphasizing that the two youngsters were not competing for one exclusive place in the team. Moore himself subsequently expressed his desire to develop a stronger understanding with El Mala ahead of October’s Rhein derby against Borussia Mönchengladbach.

The friendship also extends beyond the training ground, with El Mala revealing that his older brother Malek has spent time with Moore as well. Speaking in an extensive interview with Kicker, the 20-year-old described their growing bond.

It has been revealed that “Malek and I get on really well with Mikey,” El Mala told Kicker. “The three of us recently went out for a meal together. We get along very well. Now he’s scored his first goal after a great attacking move, which gives us confidence for the coming matches that we can play together like that. I also have a very good relationship with Linton Maina, for example, and you can see that on the pitch.”.

Cologne have struggled to translate promising performances into victories this season, but the development of their young attacking players offers encouragement. With Moore finally opening his Bundesliga account and El Mala increasingly comfortable operating in central attacking positions, Wagner will hope their growing understanding produces further rewards.

Industry observers note that musiala suffered a muscle-fibre tear while warming up for Germany’s Nations League encounter against the Netherlands in September. After gradually working his way back to fitness, the Bayern star finally returned to competitive action in last Friday’s 1-1 draw against Köln. Fußballtransfers claims Musiala’s absence will stretch out for several more weeks. Sky Germany’s Florian Plettenberg is reporting that Musiala will miss 4-6 weeks.

It has been revealed that the latest development comes during an exceptionally difficult period for Musiala, who has also been dealing with a neurological condition. Kicker and Sport Bild both report that the 23-year-old experienced another absence episode on Monday, November 23, his second reported recurrence since collapsing during August’s preparation campaign. Musiala has consequently made just six competitive appearances this season, completing the full 90 minutes on only one occasion.

In a recent development, his ongoing health difficulties have also prompted considerable discussion surrounding his future at Bayern. Honorary president Uli Hoeneß and former CEO Karl-Heinz Rummenigge recently expressed concerns about the midfielder’s ability to regain his previous performance levels. Earlier this week, Bayern also confirmed that constructive discussions had taken place with Musiala’s representatives. The club emphasized that the player’s health remained the priority and that both parties intended to continue their dialogue confidentially.

Recent findings suggest that for Kompany, Musiala’s latest absence also creates another selection headache amid a mounting injury crisis in Bayern’s attacking department. Michael Olise has also been ruled out of Saturday’s encounter with Hamburg. The French international continues to recover from bruising to his left foot sustained against Köln. Harry Kane, Serge Gnabry, and Ismael Saibari remain sidelined as well, leaving Bayern seriously depleted in attack. Luis Díaz at least returned to action against Lille following his own injury layoff.

Sono due modi diversi di avanzare. Il lavoro di Gattuso punta a mettere la squadra nelle condizioni di costruire e attaccare attraverso entrambe le corsie, in base agli uomini disponibili.

Here, Daily Mail Sport details Bellingham's lifestyle in Spain, and the rituals that have grounded the player after his explosion into superstardom.

Jude Bellingham is inching closer to a newly introduced deal at Real Madrid to become one of Europe's highest earners.

But more than just enjoying his football, Bellingham has made himself at home in the city (pictured at the Grand Prix of Spain in Madrid this year).

A recurring theme when Bellingham speaks of his love of living in Madrid stems from an established daily routine.

Speaking to his club just six months after he joined Los Blancos in the summer of 2023, Bellingham had already set up habits which helped him feel at home in the newly introduced city.

'I get up early to go to training, I train and then I head home,' Bellingham remarked. 'Sometimes I'll go out for a coffee near home or head into town to grab something to eat. Then I go back home to chill out in the garden for a bit if the weather is good and the sun's out.

'If my friends are over, we'll go out for dinner and then back home. It's great. You get to know the people at the places you visit more often. They don't see you as Jude Bellingham the footballer, but as Jude the guy who comes in for a coffee and that's great. The people I meet in the city really look after me. I feel at home.'.

Over two years later, and the patterns are no different. The Calvin Klein ambassador told Vogue this month that his ideal downtime involves 'being in the company of my friends and family, having a coffee, going for a walk.

'You're always going to get recognised, but you're a bit safer in terms of not getting mobbed,' Bellingham remarked of his favourite spots on the fringes of the city, where many of his repeat haunts are located.

Not that Bellingham is a little averse to integrating with the community. In fact, mingling with the locals has been a positive aspect of Bellingham's life abroad, with the player admitting in the summer of 2025 that Spain was very much 'home'.

In a recent development, 'When I go back to play with the national team, it's nice seeing people that I don't normally get to see – my family and friends – but I always feel more comfortable when I'm back in Madrid,' Bellingham stated in an interview with FIFA. 'It's the weather, the people are so loving, the food.

'You mix all that together, as well as, especially, playing for Real Madrid… When you go out in public and the people see you, you see it's like a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity that they've had to meet you.

It has been revealed that 'They talk to you about the club and how much it means to them. A lot of the older ladies give me kisses on the cheeks and stuff like that! It's really nice.'.

Bellingham has connected with fresh head coach Jose Mourinho since his arrival in the summer.

Shortly after his move to Madrid Bellingham moved into a villa within the upscale complex at La Finca (flats inside the community pictured).

Bellingham and his girlfriend Ashyn Castro enjoy a life of habits when together in Madrid, involving coffee walks and going out for dinner (Source: Ashlyn Castro/Instagram).

The 23-year-old lives in his mansion with his mother Denise, who often drives him to training as he is without a license.

Shortly after moving to Spain, Bellingham settled down in the exclusive La Finca neighbourhood, which plays host to a number of his team-mates including Kylian Mbappe and former club legends such as Zinedine Zidane, Cristiano Ronaldo and Iker Casillas.

The gated community is known as 'Madrid's Beverly Hills' to insiders and boasts extensive security to ensure the luxury villas inside the compound stay safe.

Bellingham is believed to have purchased his pricey six-bedroom home in 2023, moving into the complex, which boasts a home theatre, outdoor pool and gym according to Architectural Digest, with his mother Denise.

From there, his mum drives him to and from training, with the young star admitting in Vogue that despite his prodigious footballing talent, he remains borderline incapable in other aspects of life.

According to recent reports, 'I can't cook, I can't drive… I'm good at what I do, but everything else?' he joked. 'Not that great.

'I rely on my friends, my family to help me do stuff – chef, cleaner, mum, whoever else. That's where I'm at. I work hard every day and all day, and then when I get home, I've probably neglected learning how to do some of the more basic things. But there'll be a time and a place for that, I'm sure.'.

In keeping with the idea that Bellingham has found his home in Spain, it stands to reason that the player has been working on his languages.

Bellingham revealed in Vogue that he has been learning Spanish for over two years, beginning in earnest just months after his move to the Santiago Bernabeu.

Confirming his aptitude for the language, Bellingham added: 'I think a significant part of it is being confident enough to just speak.

'You know you're going to get stuff wrong, and you're probably not going to sound exactly right, (but if) people know what you're talking about, they'll probably think: "Fair play for trying".'.

Castro and Bellingham have been dating for nearly two years since early 2025, having reportedly met on exclusive dating site Raya (Source: Ashlyn Castro/Instagram).

American model Castro is a frequent fixture in the stands whether Bellingham is playing for Madrid or England.

With Bellingham settled in Madrid, his American model girlfriend Ashlyn Castro is, if not permanently based in the city, a regular visitor to both his La Finca villa and Real Madrid's home ground.

The former music video star and Bellingham have been dating since early 2025, with Castro becoming a frequent fixture at the Bernabeu alongside his mother Denise.

Castro has also been following his exploits for England too, travelling across the United States to follow the travails of Thomas Tuchel and Co as they reached the semi-finals at this summer's World Cup.

Most recently she was spotted in the stands closer to home however, with Bellingham and Castro snapped embracing after the final whistle blew on England's impressive win against Spain at Atletico Madrid's Metropolitano.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, la vittoria contro lo Stoccarda è stata importante per l'Inter non soltanto dal punto di vista sportivo, ma anche sotto il profilo economico. Il 2-0 firmato da Sucic e Lautaro Martinez ha garantito alla società nerazzurra altri 2,1 milioni di euro di premi UEFA.

L'Inter occupa il nono posto con 62,8 milioni di euro già garantiti, rispetto ai 60,7 milioni precedenti alla sfida con i tedeschi.

It has been revealed that I nerazzurri sono l'unica squadra italiana presente nella top 10, a soli 500mila euro dal Borussia Dortmund e a un milione dal Barcellona. Alle spalle della società di viale della Liberazione c'è invece il Manchester United, fermo a 58,4 milioni.

In testa alla graduatoria figura il Paris Saint-Germain con 76,2 milioni, seguito dal Real Madrid con 75,1 e dal Liverpool con 72,8.

L'Inter ha dunque ancora la possibilità di incrementare sensibilmente il proprio bottino nelle ultime tre giornate della fase campionato, sia attraverso i premi per i risultati delle singole partite sia attraverso quelli legati al piazzamento finale e all'eventuale qualificazione alla fase a eliminazione diretta.

I 62,8 milioni rappresentano quindi la cifra minima già assicurata ai nerazzurri, senza considerare gli incassi al botteghino e gli ulteriori introiti commerciali legati alla partecipazione alla Champions League.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Overpowered and overrun, Arsenal were subjected to the sort of gruelling treatment they usually inflict on their opponents. Mikel Arteta’s side did not look anything like Premier League champions here, as Brighton and Hove Albion produced a stunning performance full of swarming energy and breathless bravery.

In the biggest test of their season so far, Arsenal fell woefully short of the standards they have set themselves over the past few campaigns. This sort of thing simply does not happen to Arteta’s side. Well, it did not happen. Not before this monstering on the south coast, where the Brighton fans were whipped into a frenzy by the brilliance of Fabian Hürzeler’s players.

Brighton were everything that Arsenal are expected to be: aggressive, inventive and dominant across the field. They even scored with a set-piece, as one of Arsenal’s great strengths became a sudden weakness. Everywhere Arteta looked, the foundational truths of his team were being shaken by a Brighton storm. It was their first defeat by a three-goal margin since May 2023, also against Brighton.

Remarkably, this is now the third consecutive season in which Brighton have beaten the reigning Premier League champions. They are rarely happier than when they are on the hunt against more illustrious opponents, working as a team to snap at heels and then attacking in numbers. They are known as the Seagulls, but they played more like a pack of bloodthirsty wolves. The ferocity of their off-the-ball work, especially in the first half, was extraordinary.

According to recent reports, not for a long time have Arsenal been as rattled as they were here. David Raya misplaced passes, Gabriel Magalhães lost duels and Bruno Guimarães chased the ball in vain. It was Brighton’s Pascal Gross, rather than Arsenal’s Martin Odegaard, who shaped the game in midfield. It was Brighton’s Charalampos Kostoulas, rather than Arsenal’s Kai Havertz, who offered incisive class in attack.

Gross and Kostoulas both struck from range in a one-sided first half, before Chema Andrés added the third after the break. At half-time, Arteta had sprinted down the tunnel towards the dressing room. Whatever messages he gave to his players, they either did not sink in or did not work. By the end, Arsenal were lucky the scoreline was not even more humiliating.

Recent findings suggest that arteta’s players had come through some tricky assignments in winning their first seven matches of this season, but this was their toughest test yet and they failed it badly. They did not handle the emotions of the occasion particularly well, either: in stoppage time, a frustrated Declan Rice kicked out at Malick Yalcouyé. He was perhaps fortunate to avoid a red card.

It has been revealed that it was the first time that Rice and Guimarães had started alongside each other for Arsenal and it quickly became clear that their £180m partnership will need some work. Arsenal would have hoped their experience in the Premier League would allow for an instant connection but, evidently, that is not the case. Guimarães was hooked after 60 minutes, but might easily have been removed at the break.

According to recent reports, both managers had a similar assessment of the match and how it was won: Brighton did the basics far better than Arsenal. “How we wanted to approach this game was getting into it through small wins,” Hürzeler remarked. “Everyone speaks about a goal or chance as a win, but a small win can be the first throw-in, the first corner, win the first header, win the first tackle. These small things. If you win these small steps, and celebrate them as a win, then you can gain bigger and bigger wins.”.

It was typical of Brighton that one of their new signings produced an excellent performance in midfield. Andrés, a 21-year-old Spaniard signed from Stuttgart at the end of the transfer window, looks to be the latest gem identified by their data-led recruitment model. No one inside the Amex Stadium was thinking about Carlos Baleba, sold to Manchester United, when Andrés made his tackles and won his headers.

Another newly introduced signing, centre-back Luka Vuskovic, was similarly impressive at the back. Signed for £46m from Tottenham Hotspur, Vuskovic looks more than capable of going to the top of the game.

This was perhaps the first occasion this season in which Arsenal missed William Saliba, the injured centre-back who has been so fundamental to their success in recent years. The Frenchman can always be relied on to provide calmness and composure at the back, even under intense pressure. Without him, Arsenal were uncharacteristically jittery.

“The amount of technical errors we did in our own half...” Arteta bemoaned. “We didn’t respect any principle of play that you have to get out of those man-to-man situations. That put us always on the back foot.”.

Gross, who at 35 is playing as well as ever, opened the scoring with a low shot from range after 31 minutes. Kostoulas then struck the second, from a similar distance, after some end-to-end action resulted in Arsenal’s midfield and defence melting away. The third was the most simple, as Andrés headed in at the back post from an inswinging corner.

According to recent reports, arsenal did have some chances, with Havertz missing the best of them, but there was never a sense that Brighton were vulnerable. The pressure on the home side was never sustained. For Arteta, who now has an extended international break in which to ruminate on this defeat, it all made for an unfamiliar and unexpected pain.

Mikel Arteta remarked his Arsenal players failed to “respect the game” as their perfect start to the season was ended in stunning style by a brilliant Brighton performance.

Sources indicate that arsenal’s capitulation on the south coast led to their first defeat of the campaign and Arteta admitted that Brighton had a different “edge” and “bite” throughout the match. The Arsenal manager also remarked the 3-0 loss represented a “big lesson” for his players.

It has been revealed that “There are certain basics you need to accomplish in football, especially in the Premier League, that we were very far from,” Arteta noted. “From the first throw-in you could sense it, it was so clear.

According to recent reports, “It was a really disappointing result and performance. Brighton were another gear up from us. We were extremely poor technically and were not respecting the game.

Industry observers note that “It is not going to take away what the team has done in the last six or seven weeks since coming back from the World Cup. What we have done and the way we have competed, and the amount of games we have won, has been remarkable. But this is a substantial lesson for all of us to understand what it takes to win at this level.”.

Arteta added that his team did not “respect the principles of play” that were required against Brighton’s intense pressing, and also said his players were guilty of numerous technical errors.

In a recent development, “Credit to Brighton for what they have done because they have overcome us and they had another edge,” Arteta stated. “There are a lot of moments when the ball is 50/50 and it changes hands and most of the time it was for them.”.

Brighton are the Premier League’s top scorers this season with 16 goals in five matches so far, and this emphatic victory took them up to third place in the table.

It has been revealed that “It was a special win,” Fabian Hürzeler, the Brighton head coach, mentioned. “Not only because we played the best team in England but because of the performance. I am really proud of my team. It’s always important to enjoy these moments. We were horrible to play against. My players really trust each other on the pitch.”.

When you miss chances like we did it becomes impossible. I want to congratulate Brighton for what they’ve done. It’s a major lesson for us to learn. If I have to describe how the team has played and competed in the last six or seven weeks, has been expectational but today has been a big lesson.

We were poor technically when we had the ball in our own half, we didn’t apply the principles that you need against a team that wants to press you man to man.

The right back was due to start for Newcastle against Hull City this afternoon – his first start since April – but has picked up another injury.

Livramento only played 17 Premier League games for Newcastle last season, scuppering his chances of a summer move to Arsenal, missing huge chunks of the season with groin and hamstring issues.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of today’s Premier League 3pm kick-offs, with Brighton vs Arsenal the pick of the three matches.

Recent findings suggest that brighton are the league’s top goalscorers so far this season and have amassed the most expected goals, but the champions have the league’s best defence and are seeking five wins from five to start their title defence. There is some welcome needle between Fabian Hurzeler and Mikel Arteta, dating back to Declan Rice’s contentious second yellow for delaying the restart two years ago, as well as the Brighton manager’s comments about Arsenal’s style of play in March.

That 1-0 Arsenal victory at the Amex coincided with Man City dropping points at home to Nottingham Forest on a pivotal night in the title race. Bukayo Saka scored a deflected shot in the ninth minute, and Arsenal held on from there in an ugly but resolute display.

Industry observers note that with Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz fit and firing, as well as the introduction of Myles Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes to Arteta’s midfield stable, Arsenal’s football has been more technical and enterprising so far this season. Brighton are one of the few teams who will back themselves to play through Arsenal’s press, which should make for an absorbing game.

Sources indicate that elsewhere, Newcastle are looking to bounce back from their shellacking at Leeds at home to surprise package Hull City. Mattias Jaissle’s team took four points from Liverpool and Spurs but there is concern about how many shots they are conceding. Hull remain unbeaten and continue to confound the odds and underlying data, but that surely cannot last forever.

Everton are also one of the division’s unbeaten teams, but will be targeting three points from a home game against Ipswich after three consecutive draws. Ipswich are sitting comfortably on six points after their win at Crystal Palace, though they did have the extra man for the majority at Selhurst Park.

Gary Neville slaps himself in the FACE in bizarre on-air moment after Man United's humiliation at Anfield - weeks after claiming his old club are 'in a better place' than Liverpool

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 04:43 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:28 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • Gary Neville showcased the dramatic decline of Manchester United this season as he bizarrely slapped himself in the face on Sky Sports after his former side's 4-0, 10-man, defeat to Liverpool at Anfield.
  • Neville's dramatic example of Man United's lack of hunger and sharpness came in stark contrast to his pre-season proclamations for the side, when he informed his co-pundit Jamie Carragher that he believed that then-manager Michael Carrick's starting XI was stronger than Liverpool's after a summer recruitment drive.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 04:43 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:28 EST, 24 November 2026.

Gary Neville showcased the dramatic decline of Manchester United this season as he bizarrely slapped himself in the face on Sky Sports after his former side's 4-0, 10-man, defeat to Liverpool at Anfield.

Neville's dramatic example of Man United's lack of hunger and sharpness came in stark contrast to his pre-season proclamations for the side, when he informed his co-pundit Jamie Carragher that he believed that then-manager Michael Carrick's starting XI was stronger than Liverpool's after a summer recruitment drive.

Instead, Man United saw their numbers reduced inside the opening stages of the game after a reckless challenge by Leny Yoro, and 2-0 down after 13 minutes, with the club legend resorting to drastic methods to convey the side's weaknesses.

Of his old club's defenders, he stated: 'I never see any of them on their toes, alert, looking like they've got something fixed in here', before pointing to his head.

In a recent development, 'I never see any of them look like that,' he added. 'They look like that -'.

Neville then stared into the middle distance for a few moments to share the blankness he sees on the faces of the back line, before spitting: 'Wake up!'.

Gary Neville took to slapping himself to convey the lack of focus he sees in Man United's stars.

The club legend had previously tipped his old side to have a stronger XI than Liverpool's.

But when the two teams met at Anfield, Man United were left woefully exposed after going down to 10 men.

The Overlap broadcaster then slapped his own face a number of times repeating 'wake up!' before adding: 'You play for Man United'.

The gesture left Carragher in stitches, with the Anfield icon collapsing onto the sofa in hysterics - although less impressed with Roy Keane, who displayed his usual sangfroid.

So tickled by the moment was the former Liverpool star that he later changed his profile picture on social media site X to a still image of Neville's hand catching his face.

Neville had more sharp criticism for Man United's defensive selection assessing the inclusion of Matthijs de Ligt in the starting line-up.

The Dutch defender has been out of Premier League action for 51 weeks after suffering a back injury, but was named by Mauricio Pochettino in his first-ever XI.

'I have a lot of sympathy for him,' Neville admitted. 'It's like playing football after having six pints. It's a strange feeling.

'I have a lot of sympathy for him, it's alarming to watch.'.

Less sympathy for Man United's players came from Keane, who attacked the team - and Neville and Carragher - after the heavy defeat at Anfield confirmed the club's worst start in over 53 years.

The firebrand midfielder was on his usual caustic form as he assessed the damage, hitting out at those who might have accepted the score line, having feared a greater deficit.

Industry observers note that 'If I hear that one more time from the lads in the commentary that 4-0 is not too bad when you're down to 10 men - has a team ever got a result with 10 men before?' Keane remarked immediately after the final whistle. 'It can be done.

'I thought United were desperate. I thought they were so bad and everyone and Nev, who played for Man United saying 4-0 ain't bad.'.

'(The red card) doesn't help but you're telling me they couldn't have done better? They lost 4-0 with 10 men, that's not too bad? Has a team ever got a result with 10 men? It can be done. At least show a bit more fight, a bit more quality - I can't believe what I'm hearing from people.

'You played for the club, saying 4-0 isn't too bad. Wow. Fans are applauding. Applauding what? Performing rubbish. Liverpool were excellent, but how easy did United make it for them? I can't believe what I'm watching sometimes.

'This team two years ago finished 15th. The last year or two, we're talking. We're blaming the board, blaming ownership, blaming managers.

'When do the players take responsibility for some decision-making? Liverpool probably should have scored eight, probably eight or nine, unbelievable chances they had. And everyone's coming off the pitch saying 4 is not too bad? I feel like swearing.'.

The difference between the two teams felt a far cry from Neville's late-summer prediction, when he told Carragher that he had greater hopes for Carrick and Man United over incoming manager Andoni Iraola at Liverpool.

Recent findings suggest that 'I think Manchester United are right now in a better place than Liverpool,' Neville mentioned in August. 'Would you agree?'.

Carragher stated that he did not, and will have been confident in his assessment on Sunday night.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

L’ex portiere spiega anche perché non frequenta i social e quale momento degli allenamenti gli manca.

Secondo quanto riportato da La Repubblica, Angelo Peruzzi ha smesso di fare il dirigente della Lazio perché non si divertiva più. Lo racconta in un’intervista a La Repubblica: «Sono stato dirigente della Lazio, poi ho smesso: non mi divertivo più.».

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Peruzzi oggi vive lontano dalle apparizioni televisive. «Vivo a Blera, il mio paese in provincia di Viterbo, mi piace la campagna e stare tranquillo. Non mi annoio, le giornate volano, la vita vola», dice parlando delle sue giornate.

Industry observers note that alla domanda sul perché il calcio non gli piaccia più, Peruzzi risponde: «Non sputo nel piatto dove ho mangiato per tanto tempo, però mi domando cosa sia rimasto dentro quel piatto. Passione, a occhio poca».

Il discorso si sposta sul rapporto tra calciatori e pubblico. Peruzzi ricorda che, quando giocava, non amava concedere interviste: riteneva impossibile dire la verità senza avere problemi e pensava che questo portasse a risposte banali o a essere considerati stupidi. Poi parla dei social, assenti ai suoi tempi: «Quando giocavo, non amavo le interviste perché dire la verità era impossibile, troppe grane. E allora si diventa banali o si passa per stupidi. E non esistevano i social, questi strumenti spaventosi che hanno stravolto le nostre vite. Io non li frequento: perché mai dovrei raccontare a tutti cosa ho mangiato a colazione?».

Recent findings suggest that come riporta il Corriere dello Sport il club ha manifestato al giocatore l’intenzione di rinnovare il contratto, lo scozzese è fondamentale e anche in queste ultime gare ha dimostrato la sua importanza nella squadra di Allegri. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • La Serie A torna in campo per la 13ª giornata, in programma da venerdì 27 a lunedì 30 novembre.
  • According to recent reports, un programma ricco di partite da analizzare anche in ottica scommesse: dagli esiti finali ai mercati legati ai gol, sono diverse le possibilità per comporre una multipla.
  • Sources indicate that la prima schedina propone una combinazione che alterna una giocata più lineare a tre esiti dal profilo maggiormente rischioso.

La Serie A torna in campo per la 13ª giornata, in programma da venerdì 27 a lunedì 30 novembre. Il turno si apre con Venezia-Bologna e prosegue sabato con l’Inter di Chivu, che ospita il Genoa a San Siro. Tra le sfide del fine settimana anche Torino-Lazio e Como-Juventus, mentre il Napoli sarà impegnato sul campo del Sassuolo.

According to recent reports, un programma ricco di partite da analizzare anche in ottica scommesse: dagli esiti finali ai mercati legati ai gol, sono diverse le possibilità per comporre una multipla. Ecco la nostra schedina della 13ª giornata di Serie A, con una selezione di pronostici e quote per il weekend di campionato.

Sources indicate that la prima schedina propone una combinazione che alterna una giocata più lineare a tre esiti dal profilo maggiormente rischioso. Si parte da Venezia-Bologna, con il segno 1 quotato 3.16 da PokerStars, 3.10 da Snai e 3.15 da BetFlag, mentre in Torino-Lazio la scelta ricade sul pareggio, proposto a 3.31 da PokerStars, 3.25 da Snai e 3.30 da BetFlag. Anche in Udinese-Fiorentina viene preso in considerazione il segno X, con quote di 3.40 da PokerStars e Snai e 3.45 da BetFlag. Chiude la combinazione il successo esterno del Napoli in Sassuolo-Napoli, esito indicato a 1.66 da PokerStars, 1.65 da Snai e 1.65 da BetFlag. Una schedina che abbina quindi una selezione più coperta, come il 2 del Napoli, a risultati più complessi che contribuiscono ad alzare il valore complessivo della multipla. Nel complesso si tratta di una proposta costruita su un equilibrio particolare: da una parte un favorito abbastanza chiaro come il Napoli, dall’altra due pareggi e una vittoria interna tutt’altro che scontata. Proprio i segni X di Torino-Lazio e Udinese-Fiorentina rappresentano le giocate che possono incidere maggiormente sulla resa finale della schedina, mentre Venezia-Bologna aggiunge un ulteriore elemento di difficoltà. È una combinazione che punta quindi su una lettura meno banale del turno, con un potenziale rendimento più alto ma anche con un livello di rischio inevitabilmente superiore.

It has been revealed that la seconda schedina si apre con il segno 1 in Roma-Monza, esito considerato il più probabile dagli operatori e quotato 1.19 da PokerStars e Snai e 1.20 da BetFlag. In Como-Juventus la scelta resta ancora sul successo interno, con il segno 1 offerto a 1.97 da PokerStars, 1.95 da Snai e 2.00 da BetFlag. A seguire troviamo il pareggio in Lecce-Atalanta, proposto a 3.75 da PokerStars e Snai e 3.80 da BetFlag, mentre in Cagliari-Milan la giocata selezionata è il successo dei sardi, quotato 4.60 da PokerStars, 4.50 da Snai e 4.85 da BetFlag. Una combinazione che alterna due esiti più prudenti a due risultati dal coefficiente sensibilmente più elevato. La struttura della seconda multipla appare quindi più aggressiva nella parte finale, dove il pareggio tra Lecce e Atalanta e soprattutto il segno 1 di Cagliari-Milan alzano in modo netto il valore della schedina. Roma-Monza rappresenta la base più solida della combinazione, mentre Como-Juventus aggiunge un livello intermedio di rischio. È una schedina pensata per chi cerca una soluzione meno conservativa, nella quale i due esiti ad alta quota diventano il vero elemento distintivo dell’intera proposta.

Tornare dove tutto è cominciato, ritrovare volti e luoghi familiari per provare a lasciarsi alle spalle il momento difficile. Arthur Atta si prepara a vivere una domenica speciale, con Udine, che per due anni è stata casa sua, pronto a riaccoglierlo da avversario. Il francese sarà uno degli osservati speciali del lunch match tra Udinese e Fiorentina, in programma alle 12:30 al Bluenergy Stadium: l’obiettivo è ritrovare il campo - e magari sbloccarsi - proprio contro i suoi ex compagni, in una sfida che mette in palio punti pesantissimi in una corsa salvezza dove i viola sono ripiombati dentro con tutte le scarpe.

Recent findings suggest that arrivato a Firenze sotto grandi aspettative e accolto come il possibile colpo dell’estate, in una mattinata di luglio che aveva sorpreso tutti (compreso l’allora tecnico Fabio Grosso), Arthur Atta non è ancora riuscito a lasciare il segno in maglia viola. Il suo bilancio parla finora di zero gol e zero assist, con prestazioni al di sotto delle attese, prima che un sovraccarico funzionale all’addome, accusato durante la prima sosta per le nazionali di settembre, lo costringesse a uno stop di oltre due mesi. Dopo essere tornato tra i convocati in occasione della disastrosa trasferta di Monza, adesso il francese vuole voltare pagina. L’obiettivo è lasciarsi alle spalle le difficoltà, conquistare la fiducia del nuovo ambiente e ritagliarsi progressivamente uno spazio nelle rotazioni viola, dimostrando finalmente il proprio valore.

Recent findings suggest that tra la voglia di riscatto di Atta e il ritorno in campo, tuttavia, oltre che ad una questione fisica c'è fa fare attenzione alla nuova Fiorentina che è pronto a disegnare Paolo Vanoli. Una squadra più attenta, compatta e prudente. Dove non ci sarà spazio per tutta la qualità, soprattutto offensiva, che tifosi, dirigenti e addetti ai lavori immaginavano a inizio stagione. E a farne maggiormente le spese potrebbe esserne proprio il francese, le cui qualità sono mai state finora spiccatamente difensive. Vedremo se per lui in questa Fiorentina ci sarà spazio, intanto domenica potrebbe fargli bene l’aria di ‘casa’ per ritrovare lo smalto (e il minutaggio) perduto.

Industry observers note that 11 gol in 11 partite per Gustavo Varela, una delle rivelazioni di questo campionato. Il portoghese classe 2005 si sta mettendo in mostra con la maglia del Monza e sarà sicuramente un uomo mercato già a gennaio.

"Inter, Napoli e Juventus lo seguono, ma per trasformare l’interesse in un’operazione concreta serve un’accelerazione che al momento non c’è ancora stata. Il rischio è che, aspettando troppo, la concorrenza internazionale renda tutto più complicato. Varela sta vivendo una stagione straordinaria. Undici reti in undici partite rappresentano un impatto impressionante, soprattutto considerando il percorso con cui si sta affermando nel calcio italiano. Numeri che raccontano un giocatore capace di lasciare il segno con continuità e che inevitabilmente attirano l’attenzione delle società più ambiziose.

In a recent development, il suo nome piace a diverse substantial di Serie A. Inter, Napoli e Juventus sono attente alla sua crescita, ma al momento non si è ancora registrata un’accelerazione decisiva. È proprio questo il punto: Varela rappresenta un’occasione per tutto il calcio italiano e non soltanto per una singola società. Le dichiarazioni dei protagonisti del nostro campionato, comprese quelle di Beppe Marotta, confermano quanto il suo profilo sia apprezzato", scrive Gianluigi Longari su Sportitalia.

According to recent reports, "Il valore del giocatore ha già superato i 30 milioni di euro e potrebbe crescere ulteriormente se il Monza riuscisse a trattenerlo fino al termine della stagione. La società brianzola lo ha acquisito a titolo definitivo, consolidando una posizione importante in vista delle eventuali trattative future. Resta da considerare anche la posizione del Benfica, che secondo le informazioni circolate manterrebbe una tutela economica sull’operazione, attraverso una possibile prelazione o una percentuale sulla futura plusvalenza: un aspetto contrattuale da valutare con attenzione. Il paragone con Malen può aiutare a comprendere il tipo di impatto che un giocatore può avere quando trova l’ambiente giusto e riesce a esprimere tutto il proprio potenziale. E viene naturale tornare con la memoria anche a Diego Milito: non per stabilire equivalenze tecniche, ma per ricordare quanto il campionato italiano sappia valorizzare attaccanti capaci di incidere con continuità.

It has been revealed that le società italiane, però, devono essere consapevoli di un rischio: se continueranno a limitarsi a osservare, potrebbero lasciare spazio ai club della Premier League. Con la disponibilità economica di cui dispongono le società inglesi, una trattativa potrebbe diventare rapidamente fuori portata per le nostre big. Per questo Inter, Napoli e Juventus devono capire se Varela sia davvero un obiettivo e, in caso affermativo, muoversi per tempo", chiosa poi il giornalista.

Ieri sera il Milan ha completato la rimonta con un contropiede orchestrato dal solito Hutchinson, rifinito da Pulisic e finalizzato da Moreira. Primo gol europeo per Diego con la maglia rossonera e punteggio fissato sul 2-4. Nella sua esultanza Diego Moreira è andato a "sfidare" la caldissima curva dell'Olympiacos guardandola con sguardo fisso e serio, prima di mimare il gesto del "toc toc" e con un calcio sfondare la porta immaginaria. Un'esultanza che non è piaciuta ad alcuni giocatori della squadra greca (e ai tifosi), che si sono scagliati contro il giocatore milanista, e che negli strascichi post-gara sta generando un po' di polemiche francamente esagerate.

Industry observers note that A riportare l'attenzione sull'esultanza di Diego Moreira nel post gara è stata una domanda rivolta da un collega della stampa greca a Ruben Amorim in conferenza stampa: il tecnico rossonero a quel punto ha sentito il bisogno di scusarsi con il pubblico e club greco, gesto comunque onorevole e da sottolineare da parte sua, ma allo stesso tempo ha giustamente difeso l'intento del suo calciatore che non era certo così grave come sta venendo dipinto in queste ore. Queste le parole di Amorim: "Non succederà più. Moreira è un ragazzo che vive come gioca, ma deve crescere. Sappiamo che non ci piacerebbe se lo facessero con i nostri tifosi. È una mia responsabilità, ma non l'ha fatto in maniera cattiva. Chiedo scusa, ma non l'ha fatto in maniera cattiva".

Diciamocelo chiaramente. Sicuramente, come ha sottolineato Ruben Amorim, Diego Moreira poteva magari evitare un'esultanza un po' provocatoria, ma allo stesso tempo non è sembrato essere un modo di festeggiare tanto più esuberante di molti che si sono visti sui campi da calcio nella storia di questo sport. Comprensibile, al termine di una gara così, il nervosismo dei giocatori greci, per carità: ma il campo ha offerto talmente tanti spunti e talmente tanto spettacolo da un lato e dall'altro, che ridursi a parlare solamente dell'esultanza di Moreira sul quarto gol pare una forzatura. Dal canto suo Diego Moreira, che fino a questo momento ha comunque avuto un atteggiamento sempre mai sopra le righe, può fare tesoro di questa esperienza come suggerito da Amorim, anche per evitare conseguenze spiacevoli: è un ragazzo intelligente e sicuramente lo avrà capito. Per il resto, per il clima caldo che c'è stato per tutti i 90 minuti, questo è un tema che poteva rimanere tranquillamente una "cosa di campo". Nient'altro da aggiungere.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Il workshop intende ribadire quanto già illustrato nel primo tavolo, tenutosi lo scorso 6 ottobre: il diabete non rappresenta alcun limite nel poter fare sport,.

Si terrà oggi alle 18 il secondo seminario del ciclo ‘Diabete in Libertà – Sport e Diabete’, fortemente voluto dalla Fondazione Lazio ETS, avente come focus il rapporto tra sport e diabete. L’incontro, realizzato in collaborazione con ANIAD, l’Associazione Nazionale Italiana Atleti Diabetici e AMD, Associazione Medici Diabetologi, si svolgerà con due modalità: in presenza nella Torretta di Piazza della Libertà e anche on line tramite zoom.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

According to recent reports, il numero 1 al mondo del tennis, ha avuto la sua prima diagnosi di diabete nel 2001, a soli 4 anni. Il campione tedesco ha reso nota la sua condizione nel 2022.A illustrare ai partecipanti tutte le possibilità che la scienza e la medicina mettono a disposizione dei soggetti affetti da diabete, sarà il professor Felice Strollo, specialista in Endocrinologia e docente di Medicina Aeronautica e Spaziale. Strollo attualmente ricopre anche il ruolo di Membro del Comitato Scientifico dell'ANIADIl seminario odierno è rivolto a tutti i pazienti, agli addetti ai lavori e non solo a sportivi professionisti. L’obiettivo è chiaro: far comprendere che con il diabete si può convivere serenamente, fare sport e condurre una vita senza alcun tipo di condizionamento.

Il seminario avrà luogo oggi alle 18 presso la Torretta di Piazza della Libertà. Per favorire la massima partecipazione, sarà possibile accedere anche tramite Zoom. L’ID riunione è 896 06 29 3452, il codice d’accesso è 929913.

Spitting row mars feisty Millwall-West Ham clash

📅 19 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5391 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A spitting row marred the 100th Millwall-West Ham United derby and first for 14 years.
  • Taty Castellanos was facing trial by video after being accused of spitting on Filip Marschall during Saturday’s febrile 2-2 draw at the Den.
  • Millwall goalkeeper Marschall made the allegation to referee Paul Tierney, who was expected to include it in an official report that would then be assessed by the Football Association.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A spitting row marred the 100th Millwall-West Ham United derby and first for 14 years.

Taty Castellanos was facing trial by video after being accused of spitting on Filip Marschall during Saturday’s febrile 2-2 draw at the Den.

Millwall goalkeeper Marschall made the allegation to referee Paul Tierney, who was expected to include it in an official report that would then be assessed by the Football Association.

Spitting on an opponent is punishable with a six-match ban.

Telegraph Sport has been told West Ham striker Castellanos denies he spat on Marschall and believes he will be vindicated by video footage of the incident.

Industry observers note that lying little prick. Taty didn't spit ❌ pic.twitter.com/5vYxOtKqof.

Millwall manager Alex Neil mentioned after the game that fourth official Lewis Smith had confirmed a spitting accusation had been made.

According to recent reports, asked if he had spoken to Marschall about the claim, Neil replied: “I haven’t asked him about it. But it’s like anything else; I’m sure there’ll be footage of it, or not of it, if it didn’t happen.

“I’d be extremely surprised if Fil’s made an accusation and nothing’s happened. But that’s not really for me to deal with; I’m sure the authorities will deal with that.”.

According to recent reports, west Ham manager Nuno Espírito Santo said: “I’m aware of the allegation. I didn’t see the image; I didn’t speak with Taty. I cannot go much further on that.”.

He added: “I’m going to try to look at the images.”.

There were also ugly scenes at full time when players had to be separated at the end of a derby that had been at the centre of an unprecedented police operation.

There were six arrests as of 4pm on Saturday for offences including tailgating, assault on a police officer and entering or attempting to enter a stadium while intoxicated.

Eleven men were also arrested at around 7.15pm on Friday on suspicion of conspiracy to commit criminal damage.

The group, believed to be Millwall fans, were detained in the vicinity of a known West Ham supporters’ pub in Stratford.

Saturday’s fixture was subject to a five-mile dispersal zone, the largest ever for a football match in London, with officers granted special powers to stop and search people and vehicles without reasonable suspicion and to remove anyone causing disorder.

Riot police were out in force outside the ground, with dog units and mounted officers among 400 personnel deployed – roughly quadruple the usual number for a game there.

Those and other measures – including the use of live facial recognition, a strict segregation policy and a 12.30pm kick-off to minimise supporters’ pre-match drinking time – prevented a repeat of the kind of violence which has marred this fixture down the years.

West Ham fans also received a police escort to a game that saw both sets of supporters hurl foul-mouthed insults at each other throughout.

Looks to keep rival spectators apart after the match were reportedly tested by scuffles that broke out as people left the ground.

If the police were ready for a fight before the game, West Ham’s players were not as Millwall tore into them from the first whistle and dominated a first half in which they scored twice through Caleb Taylor and Camiel Neghli and hit the crossbar through a stunning 35-yard strike by Mark Sykes.

Sources indicate that MILLWALL STRIKE FIRST 🔥Caleb Taylor fires the Lions in front! pic.twitter.com/pPffYZD73D.

However, the Championship leaders finally turned up in the second half and pulled a goal back through Mohamadou Kanté before Konstantinos Mavropanos equalised with just 10 minutes to go.

ALL SQUARE at the Den 🙌West Ham equalise in the 80th minute.Everything to play for with just 10 minutes remaining 👀 pic.twitter.com/qQmDlyuQmT.

That was only after Marschall gestured that he had been spat at by Castellanos following a melee in the penalty area.

Tierney did, though, brandish a red card when Kanté pulled back Kyrell Lisbie as the substitute robbed him of the ball on the halfway line and ran clean through on goal.

The foul denied Lisbie the chance to hand Millwall their first win over their bitter rivals for 22 years, much to the frustration of fans who had roared them on from first whistle to last.

RED CARD 🟥West Ham are down to ten men, after Kante was sent off for denial of a goalscoring opportunity. pic.twitter.com/jRlVwLNiOs.

Describing the atmosphere as “absolutely the best by far” since he joined the club almost two years ago, Neil said: “I told the players prior to the game that this game’s a real rarity and, as a player and as a manager, it’s a privilege to be part of it.”.

Millwall: Marschall; Osei-Tutu, Taylor, Cooper, Sturge; Metcalfe (Servais 81), Mazou-Sacko (Cundle 90); Sykes (Baggott 70), Dykes, Neghli; Arconte (Lisbie 81).Booked: Lisbie 90+5.Goals: Taylor 16, Neghli 45+3.Subs not used: Batth, Crocombe, Doughty, Issoufou, Kelly.West Ham United: Hermansen; Walker-Peters (Kanté 46), Mavropanos, Kilman, Morato; Bowen, Engels, Mukasa (Austbo 68), Solomon; Piroe (Pablo 46), Castellanos (Orford 90).Booked: Morato 40, Pablo 83, Kilman 86, Mavropanos 90+5.Sent off: Kanté 89.Goals: Kanté 74, Mavropanos 80.Subs not used: Ajala, Austbo, Golambeckis, Herrick, Magassa, Scarles.Referee: Paul Tierney.

Sources indicate that 🗣️ "We started to tire in the second half"Millwall manager Alex Neil shares his thoughts on this afternoon's Dockers Derby, after the Lions drew 2-2 with West Ham. pic.twitter.com/xnmubZ9NIz.

Industry observers note that 🗣️ 'We were able to bounce back, but we need to look at the things we have not done so well'Nuno Espirito Santo reflects on West Ham's performance after the Hammers fought back from 2-0 down to draw with Millwall. pic.twitter.com/NM1wQVcN0o.

Asked by Sky Sports for his view on the “spitting” incident, Alex Neil said: “Fil [Marschall] was saying to the referee throughout the game when that happened at that point... Obviously I’m so far away it’s hard for me to see what happened, but I wouldn’t presume that Fil would say that without cause.

“I’m sure the referee and authorities who need to deal with it will look at it and, if it warrants it, it needs dealt with and then I’m sure they will.”.

"It's one of the best atmospheres I've ever played in..I got shivers walking out"Millwall's Caleb Taylor speaks to Aaron Paul following today's 2-2 draw with West Ham. pic.twitter.com/yFoRuxooe6.

In a recent development, will there be one final chance? Sturge earns a throw-in on the far side and Dykes limbers up... But West Ham clear their lines and that is that. It ends two goals apiece.

Recent findings suggest that lisbie has looked dangerous down that left side and he just runs out of room under pressure from Mavropanos. The pair square up, with Lisbie sticking his finger into the Greek’s cheek.

Lisbie darts to the by-line but his cutback does not make it through the thicket of limbs and West Ham clear their lines.

Millwall earn a free-kick to the left of the box as Mavropanos climbs all over Dykes. Servais picks out Baggott at the far post and his knock-down lands to Dykes who, will spinning, strikes the ball over the bar.

DYKES! 😱So close to a late winner for Millwall, but his shot flies over the bar. pic.twitter.com/fQFpQBdS7j.

Neghli steps up to take it but it strikes the wall.

There will be five minutes of time added on...

Woah.. Kante gets his pocket picked by Lisbie on the half-way line and the West Ham goalscorer has no choice but to foul him as the last man. West Ham have a free-kick just outside the box.

RED CARD 🟥West Ham are down to ten men, after Kante was sent off for denial of a goalscoring opportunity. pic.twitter.com/jRlVwLNiOs.

In a recent development, millwall have put so much into this and it’s starting to tell. Their players look leggy and aren’t able to track Kante’s run into the channel though Cooper is just about able to clear his lines. Bowen’s corner comes to nothing.

According to recent reports, pablo’s at it again, steaming his way into the left half-space, but Mazou-Sacko does well to track back and block the Brazilian’s effort. The resulting corner is gathered by Marschall who attempts to send Servais away but Kilman is wise to it and takes a booking for a professional foul.

Mazou-Sacko has his hands all over Pablo’s back and while the Brazilian is awarded a free-kick he slams the ball to the ground feeling he had broken free. He earns a booking for his troubles and the resulting free-kick comes to nothing.

Millwall 2 West Ham 2 (Mavropanos) Millwall are finally undone by a cross. Bowen goes short with a corner and Solomon dinks the ball on to the Greek defender’s head and he plants the ball past Marschall. The away end erupts...

ALL SQUARE at the Den 🙌West Ham equalise in the 80th minute.Everything to play for with just 10 minutes remaining 👀 pic.twitter.com/qQmDlyuQmT.

It’s Bowen’s turn to try an effort at goal. Metcalfe does brilliantly to charge it down but there is no respite for Millwall as Kante’s long-range sighter goes behind for another corner.

That goal has changed the dynamic of this match. Millwall have dropped into a back five and West Ham are all over them. Bowen earns his side a corner and his delivery comes out to Solomon on the edge of the box, and while Cooper is able to partially clear, Austbo stings the gloves of Marschall from distance to win another corner.

Millwall 2 West Ham 1 (Kante) The substitute strokes a right-footed effort into the bottom corner from outside the box. A great finish.

GOAL for West Ham!Kante finds the back of the net with a clinical finish from outside the box.Can the Hammers draw level? pic.twitter.com/0RZO8oqrtR.

Bowen hangs up a corner but Millwall clear their lines with ease. The hosts look so comfortable defending balls into the box.

Sources indicate that the versatile defender Baggott is on for Sykes. ITV have just shown a replay of the “spitting” incident but it’s really difficult to make anything out from that distance.

Sources indicate that the resulting corner comes to nothing. ITV are relaying reports of a counter-claim from Millwall that Castellanos might have spat in Marschall’s direction.

According to recent reports, chance! Bowen stands up a delightful cross and Pablo forces Marschall into a fine stop. Corner awarded.

Austbo replaces Mukasa for West Ham.

Some confusion here as Marschall appears to have taken too long over a goal-kick, and while most believe that a West Ham corner had been awarded, it ends up being a goal-kick.

The ITV commentators say that West Ham are alleging that Marschall spat in Pablo’s direction.

It has been revealed that arconte chases down a lost cause and telescopes a leg through Taylor to earn a corner. He spins around to the home supporters and windmills his arms in their direction as the volume increases. Metcalfe’s cross is well overhit, though, and sails out for a goal-kick.

Kante’s runs in behind are threatening to disrupt Millwall’s backline shape, but Neil’s midfield sentries Mazou-Sacko and Metcalfe are doing such a great job to cover the gaps that the hosts still look like they have things under control.

A thunderous chant of “Milllllllll” echoes around the ground as the home fans spur their charges on.

Oof. Metcalfe leaves a foot in on Morato, his studs going into the defender’s Achilles. He should perhaps consider himself lucky to avoid punishment there. One that VAR may have intervened on in the Premier League.

Penalty shout! Metcalfe drives forward into the right of the box and Kante, who is hot pursuit, pushes the midfielder to the ground. Tierney immediately waves away the appeals and replays concur that the contact is probably not strong enough to warrant a penalty.

Bowen is presented with some grass to run into but his cross is well cleared. He gets another bite at the cherry, trying his luck from the edge of the box and Marschall just about gets to the rebound ahead of an onrushing Kante. A corner is awarded which the Millwall stopper flaps at but his team-mates are able to avert the danger.

West Ham earn a chance to deliver a corner from the near side but Engel’s inswinger finds Marschall’s gloves. Really poor.

Millwall continue leveraging Cooper and Taylor’s height in the box off set-pieces. Here, Metcalfe’s free-kick skims off the top of Cooper’s head but just misses the mark.

Two changes from Nuno, who takes off Piroe and Walker-Peters for Pablo and Kante.

Sources indicate that millwall have been good value for their lead, taking 16 shots and creating three massive chances. West Ham, conversely have managed just one shot, off-target, despite controlling two-thirds of possession.

Arne Engel’s heatmap suggests he’s spent most of the match inside or just in advance of West Ham’s defensive third, which is not where Nuno will want either him or Divine Mukasa. The West Ham head coach could be tempted into changes at the break.

It has been revealed that this is no more than Millwall – and West Ham – deserve. Sykes’s outrageous 35-yard strike deserved a goal and Neghli makes sure justice is served on the stroke of half-time. The roar that greets the players leaving the field is deafening.

Recent findings suggest that the Den is in dreamland. Millwall take a two-goal advantage into the break and Neil celebrates with unbridled delight on the touchline. A caveat, though... Millwall did spurn a 2-0 lead in their most recent match away at Middlesbrough.

Millwall 2 West Ham 0 (Neghli) It’s come from yet another Dykes long throw, which West Ham have failed to clear. The ball falls to the feet of Neghli in the six-yard box and he spears the ball beyond Hermansen and Bowen on the line. And that’s the half.

Millwall, for the umpteenth time, find themselves in a two-vs-two situation on the beak, as Arconte tries to twist Kilman one way and then the other. He sets the ball to Metcalfe but the contact is not great and Hermansen gathers.

West Ham threaten Millwall’s lead momentarily as Mukasa breaks down their right, but Marschall does well to smother the ball and earns a free-kick on the process.

In an attempt to get his foot on the ball, Engels has often peeled out to the right-back position, but a wild, desperate cross-field ball that goes straight to Osei-Tutu sums up West Ham’s half aptly.

West Ham’s strength comes from the fluidity of their front four, but Nuno’s creators have not been able to access them. So effective has Millwall’s back-line coverage been that West Ham have only managed low-quality final-third entries.

According to recent reports, millwall are going man-to-man as West Ham try to build and the visitors are struggling to get out. Sturge works infield from his starting perch on the left and almost threads a through-ball in behind for Arconte to gallop on to but Kilman does well to stick in a boot.

Industry observers note that west Ham are desperately trying to calm this game down, but the Millwall fans are making that quite the challenge. The visitors string a series of passes together before Bowen strays offside.

Millwall then burst forward, Arconte this time popping up in a dangerous position on the right but Metcalfe fires over having picked off a loose Hammers pass out from the back.

Recent findings suggest that another Dykes throw-in sparks panic in West Ham’s box. Osei-Tutu’s back-post header appears to take a deflection off Walker-Peters, but the referee awards a goal-kick.

Hermansen gets caught in no-man’s land as Millwall spin in another ball from deep. It falls to the feet of Dykes but his effort does not have the requisite power to beat Kilman on the line.

Mavropanos appears to have been taken out by his own goalkeeper in the commotion and receives some on-field medical treatment.

Kevin Nolan, West Ham’s captain, was sent off early but his team-mates defied the odds to win 2-1 thanks to goals from Carlton Cole and Winston Reid either side of a stunning Liam Trotter strike.

In Millwall’s match-day squad that day were… Harry Kane and Ryan Mason.

The last time West Ham and Millwall met, Harry Kane was a Millwall player 😅This is how that game in 2012 played out 👇 pic.twitter.com/OhtVx3caCP.

This rivalry was forged in different circumstances from most derby confrontations. There is none of the religious divide of Celtic and Rangers, or the politics of Barcelona against Real Madrid, or the spat over title-winning superiority of Manchester United and Liverpool. This is a tale of proximity, an internecine feud.

Recent findings suggest that “There’s no politics, no nationality, nothing like that,” claims Nick Hart, who hosts the weekly podcast Achtung! Millwall. “We’re very similar people, from the same backgrounds, same communities. But it’s in the Millwall supporter’s DNA for West Ham to be the ultimate rivals. Nobody else comes into the equation. You’re brought up on this stuff. It’s your history.”.

Though possibly more recent history than might be suggested by the two clubs’ early foundations. The hostility that West Ham will face at the Den is no more about dockland rivalry, north-south London disputes or strike-breaking than the animosity when Manchester United visit Anfield is caused by the building of the Manchester Ship Canal.

In a recent development, “It really is about the hooligan era,” claims a podcaster who uses the pseudonym Former West Ham Employee on the West Ham Way podcast. “The two clubs had notorious fanbases. And they grated. It came about through vying to be the No 1, battling to see who had the hardest mob. Whenever we’ve played – or even been in close proximity – things have happened.”.

Jake Cooper on making the 500th appearance of his career against West Ham today! 👏Watch all the action with NOW! https://t.co/56JOZ0NPsr pic.twitter.com/lTzXOwXhxd.

Sources indicate that there have only been 18 meetings between these fierce rivals since the Second World War, but absence has certainly not made the heart grow fonder. Here are some of the feud’s most notable flashpoints.

At the 1972 testimonial in honour of Harry Cripps – the renowned Millwall hard man – police horses were sent on to the pitch after West Ham supporters entered the home section at The Den. Fighting spilt over into the streets surrounding the ground.

An even bleaker turn came in 1976, when Millwall fan Ian Pratt died in a skirmish with West Ham fans at New Cross station that led to his fall under a train.

Leaflets were later handed out in the Den’s Cold Blow Lane end with a grainy picture of Pratt and a declaration in capital letters: “A West Ham fan must die next week to avenge him.”.

Millwall plundered four goals on Mothering Sunday in 2004 as Tim Cahill’s double helped them to a 4-1 victory over West Ham at the Den in an incident-filled derby.

Industry observers note that the hosts missed a penalty and had another saved by Stephen Bywater, who was later sent off. Violence followed in the stands and the match was named “The Mothers’ Day Massacre”.

Mother's Day Massacre ⏮️A 4-1 victory over The Hammers back in 2004. pic.twitter.com/TLi7xkcVJG.

A hundred West Ham and Millwall supporters clashed during a screening of England’s 2006 World Cup match against Paraguay in Canada Square, which led to 16 injuries and one hospitalisation.

The clubs’ League Cup meeting in 2009 at Upton Park was listed as Category Five by police, the most serious risk of violence, and resulted in a Millwall supporter being stabbed in Priory Road, near the ground.

The Metropolitan Police stated that “planned” scuffles, which involved more than 100 fans, appeared to have been caused by fans without tickets to the game.

Sources indicate that just spotted one Millwall fan outside the ground in blue boxing gloves. He is also wearing what appear to be slippers, so not sure what that means….

Nuno Espirito Santo has only been through the door at West Ham for a matter of months, but he insisted he is fully aware of the significance of today’s fixture.

It has been revealed that when asked about his perception of the rivalry, Nuno mentioned: “Since the fixture list came out, this date has been [vital], for both of the clubs. It’s special, special game. We look forward to go and compete against a good team.

“It’s a different game from all of the other games, it’s a special game, the atmosphere will be different… Steve [Potts, first-team coach and former West Ham player] has been involved in many of these games, he’s constantly speaking about how special it is for West Ham fans, so we have a lot of information and we are fully aware of the importance of the game.

According to recent reports, on potential unrest between fans and the significant police presence, Nuno added: “What we want most is that everything goes well, both fans supporting their teams and no conflict. We have people inside the club who are taking care of that. We have to focus on our tasks.”.

The gaffer on tomorrow's fixture ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/6NG6t4t4Fn.

#westham on the way to #millwall via #london bridge #whufc #coyi pic.twitter.com/HrWgJ6UtJY.

It has been revealed that riot police are very much out in force outside The Den today for the 100th competitive derby between Millwall and West Ham United and first for 14 years. Dog units and mounted officers can been seen patrolling the perimeter of the ground, with 400 personnel deployed to stop violence erupting between rival fans – roughly quadruple the usual number for a fixture here. There has been no sign of any trouble with less than an hour to go before kick-off.

In a recent development, the game has been scheduled for 12.30pm to minimise supporters’ pre-match drinking time, although plenty of fans have been nursing pints before entering the ground. Other measures in place include the use of live facial recognition cameras, while a dispersal order has been imposed covering a large area around the stadium. Police were also planning to escort West Ham fans from South Bermondsey station, which will also be closed to home supporters for up to an hour after full-time. The latter measure has been deemed safer than holding the 1,800 away fans back following the game.

The Millwall-West Ham derby is one of the most notorious in English football and was most recently marred by serious violence when the sides met at Upton Park for a League Cup tie back in 2009. One man was stabbed and the match itself was interrupted on three occasions by fans invading the pitch.

Alex Neil switches out goalkeeper Max Crocombe for Filip Marschall and names the returning Mathis Servais, Kyrell Lisbie and Alfie Doughty on the bench.

The Metropolitan Police will have 400 officers on the streets of east London for this match – about four times the norm for a Championship fixture – and it has enforced a Section 35 dispersal order in the area highlighted on the map below.

A Section 35 order authorises a Police Constable and a Police Community Support Officer in uniform to “exclude a person from an area for a period of up to 48 hours with an Inspector’s authority”.

Recent findings suggest that good morning and welcome to our live coverage of the highly anticipated Championship match between Millwall and West Ham United as the two clubs meet officially for the 100th time. This fixture has not been staged since 2012, and the intervening 14 years have done little to temper the ill-feeling between their passionate supporters, who will be anxious to claim bragging rights over their Dockers Derby rivals. The Metropolitan Police have placed a Section 35 dispersal order in the area surrounding The Den and will deploy 400 officers on the streets of east London.

Industry observers note that acrimony between the two clubs has existed since the late 19th century when Millwall Athletic, originally Rovers, battled it out against Thames Ironworks, later renamed West Ham at the Athletic and Memorial Grounds. Sixty of the two clubs’ 99 meetings came between 1899 and 1915, and while they played just seven times between 1946 and 1987, the irregularity of the game only added to its mystique, which has often spilt over into the ugly.

Both head coaches spoke at length about the significance of today’s match, with Alex Neil, in the Millwall dugout, describing it as an encounter that means “absolutely everything” but imploring his players to keep “cool heads”. His counterpart Nuno Espírito Santo revealed that he had been well advised about the game’s importance by Steve Potts, his first-team coach and former West Ham player.

Sources indicate that since the club’s last meeting in 2012, West Ham have ascended into the Premier League, moved into the London Stadium and won the Uefa Conference League, only falling back into England’s second tier last summer where Millwall have remained for all but two seasons. The Lions brushed maddeningly close to promotion in their last campaign as they pushed for an automatic spot until the very last weekend of the regular season before falling to Hull City in the play-off semi-finals.

Industry observers note that much of the pre-match talk will centre on the clubs’ long-standing rivalry, but beneath the bile and belligerence is an intriguing football match between two sides. Millwall are missing 11 first-team players and face the daunting task of stopping a West Ham side who have found their feet in the Championship, scoring 16 goals in their last four league matches.

Breaking: Pisa, Bianco: "Ad Arezzo per dare continuità. Ho sbagliato i cambi col Modena"

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1559 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tuttomercatoweb

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Il Pisa cerca continuità dopo i quattro punti conquistati nelle ultime due gare contro Empoli e Modena.
  • Che partita si aspetta contro l'Arezzo, anche alla luce del recente cambio di allenatore?
  • Il rendimento casalingo è diverso rispetto a quello in trasferta, soprattutto per quanto riguarda i gol subiti.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Il Pisa cerca continuità dopo i quattro punti conquistati nelle ultime due gare contro Empoli e Modena. Domenica, nella 14ª giornata di Serie B, i nerazzurri saranno impegnati sul campo dell'Arezzo, avversario reduce dal cambio in panchina dopo l'esonero di Cristian Bucchi e la nomina di Fabio Caserta. Alla vigilia della sfida, il tecnico nerazzurro Paolo Bianco ha fatto il punto della situazuione nella consueta conferenza stampa. Queste le sue parole:.

Che partita si aspetta contro l'Arezzo, anche alla luce del recente cambio di allenatore? "Mi aspetto ad Arezzo che diamo continuità alla prestazione di Modena. Sia a Empoli che con il Modena abbiamo raccolto quattro punti, potevano essere sei. Abbiamo fatto due ottime prestazioni contro l'ultima e contro la squadra che, a detta dei risultati e di tanti addetti ai lavori, è la più in forma del campionato. In tutta la partita non abbiamo mai dato la sensazione di essere fuori dal match. Poi naturalmente non l'abbiamo vinta per motivi che ben sappiamo. Per quanto riguarda il cambio dell'allenatore dell'Arezzo, arriva un tecnico che conosco molto bene perché è stato un mio ex compagno di squadra in due squadre. È un ragazzo che stimo tantissimo. Fabio Caserta è un allenatore camaleontico, nel senso che in ogni situazione cambia sistema in base alle caratteristiche dei calciatori che ha a disposizione. Dovremo essere molto bravi a capire velocemente che partita sarà. Anche per me, per il mio staff e per i nostri analisti sarà uno stimolo, perché dovremo sopperire al fatto di non avere informazioni tattiche precise prima di giocare".

Il rendimento casalingo è diverso rispetto a quello in trasferta, soprattutto per quanto riguarda i gol subiti. Come spiega questa differenza? "È un dato che pesa sulla classifica, perché penso che in almeno due gare, ma anche nell'ultima, avessimo la possibilità, per quello che abbiamo dimostrato, di portare a casa la posta in palio piena. Con quattro punti in più saremmo in una situazione di classifica diversa. I punti che ci mancano sono quelli che abbiamo lasciato per strada in casa, perché fuori casa il nostro cammino è quello di una squadra solida, importante. In casa abbiamo toppato più di qualche volta, a partire dalla prima di campionato, nella quale secondo me non meritavamo la sconfitta. Poi c'è stata la partita balorda contro l'Entella e questi tre pareggi di cui parlavo".

Industry observers note that domani i tifosi potranno assistere all'allenamento. Quanto è importante la loro vicinanza? E il 4-4-2 o 4-4-1-1 può essere il sistema da cui ripartire? "Per quanto riguarda i tifosi, domani al campo io, se potessi, li farei venire sempre, tutti i giorni. Naturalmente per tanti motivi non è fattibile. La loro vicinanza prima della trasferta di Empoli, fuori dai cancelli del centro sportivo, è stata qualcosa che mi ha emozionato. Domani sarà ancora più bello perché assisteranno al nostro allenamento di rifinitura. È una cosa che secondo me bisognerebbe fare più spesso. Per quanto riguarda il sistema di gioco, dipende dai momenti. Avevamo preso una strada, poi personalmente pensavo non fosse quella giusta, l'abbiamo cambiata e poi abbiamo ricambiato. Più che altro perché abbiamo tanti giocatori di qualità in attacco e mi piace farne giocare quanti più possibili. È normale, però, che gli stessi giocatori offensivi debbano aiutarci nella fase di non possesso. Se riescono a sacrificarsi quando la palla è in possesso degli avversari, allora si può fare qualsiasi cosa. Sono proprio loro a determinare un po' il sistema: io farei giocare sempre quanti più giocatori di qualità offensivi possibili, perché si divertono di più a giocare insieme. Quando la palla ce l'hanno gli avversari, però, dobbiamo essere bravi a mantenere l'equilibrio".

Industry observers note that il Pisa ha subito diversi gol, spesso anche dopo essere passato in vantaggio. Come si può migliorare nella gestione delle partite? "Abbiamo subito tanti gol, ma il calcio sta andando in una direzione diversa. La gente vuole assistere a partite diverse rispetto a qualche anno fa, quando si giocavano troppe partite statiche. Con il tempo effettivo si gioca di più e questo permette, di conseguenza, anche di subire più gol. Se andiamo a vedere tutte le partite di coppa e i campionati professionistici europei, si segna di più e, di conseguenza, si subiscono più gol. Naturalmente a me non fa piacere subirne tanti, però più o meno tutte le squadre subiscono più reti rispetto agli altri anni".

Si aspetta nuove rotazioni nella formazione titolare in vista dell'Arezzo? "Vediamo, perché siamo ancora a 48 ore dalla gara. Abbiamo tutto il tempo per valutare meglio. Le 48 ore sono il momento peggiore per scegliere una formazione, soprattutto per quanto riguarda le valutazioni post partita".

It has been revealed that quanto è importante Stefano Moreo nello sviluppo della manovra offensiva? Ci sono altri giocatori che possono ricoprire quel ruolo? "Stefano ha caratteristiche diverse da tutti gli altri giocatori che avete nominato, perché ha struttura e qualità. Ha sbagliato un po' troppo tecnicamente rispetto alle sue qualità, ma è l'unico che può fare tutto: se la palla è più alta riesce a fare la sponda di testa, se gli è addosso riesce a proteggerla e, se riesce a pulirla, può giocare nella maniera giusta. Stefano è un giocatore con caratteristiche uniche. Naturalmente può giocarci anche qualcun altro, ma cambiano le caratteristiche e quindi cambierebbe anche lo sviluppo di quella situazione".

Sources indicate that contro il Modena si è parlato anche del contributo di Marras. È stata la sua migliore prestazione? "Su Marras penso una cosa: determina. È il calciatore che, quando entra e gioca dall'inizio, calcia più di tutti. Ha già fatto cinque gol giocando meno degli altri. È un giocatore determinante sotto l'aspetto dei tiri, degli assist e dei gol e lo dimostra il suo score fino a questo momento. Anche l'altro giorno ha fatto un lavoro importante: nel primo tempo ha quasi difeso da mezzala. Quello che ha fatto lui e quello che fa Moreo sono esempi del sacrificio che chiedo ai nostri giocatori offensivi. Moreo, quando è in campo, a volte può essere meno pulito e meno lucido, ma anche perché svolge un lavoro difensivo che fanno pochi centrocampisti in generale".

In a recent development, contro il Modena ci sono stati alcuni interventi che avrebbero potuto portare a espulsioni. Serve maggiore attenzione sotto questo aspetto? "Sono d'accordo. Abbiamo rischiato sia su un intervento di Loyola che su quello di Medina. Il campo non aiuta, ma oggi è molto complicato giocare a calcio perché, in base a come metti il piede e tocchi la caviglia o la gamba dell'avversario, rischi un cartellino rosso. In quei due casi abbiamo rischiato tanto e sarebbe stato complicato portare a termine la gara. Dobbiamo essere consapevoli di queste situazioni e gestirle meglio. Il Modena ha costruito una squadra molto intelligente. Conosco i dirigenti e so come lavorano. Hanno fatto una squadra sulla quale puntano, anche se magari non lo dicono apertamente, e sono consapevoli delle proprie qualità. Noi dobbiamo raggiungere quella stessa consapevolezza, che ci permetta di stare nella partita come abbiamo fatto contro il Modena e contro le squadre più forti, almeno sulla carta, di questo campionato".

Dopo l'errore di Isaac sul gol del Modena, teme che il giocatore possa perdere fiducia nelle proprie qualità? "Quella non è una situazione che riguarda un principio di gioco: era una punizione sotto la panchina e, se la squadra sale, devono salire tutti. Non è un'accusa a Isaac, naturalmente. Ha fatto una scelta sbagliata, lui è il primo che lo sa, il primo che non ci ha dormito e il primo che sta male. Io non chiedo alla squadra di salire e a Isaac di giocare la palla da solo. È una situazione nella quale ha preso una decisione individuale, ma è un'esperienza che ha vissuto e che non ripeterà. I più giovani possono imparare e diventare più forti anche sbagliando. Ci sono momenti della gara nei quali, anche se l'allenatore chiede di fare qualcosa, poi è il giocatore a dover scegliere. Eravamo in vantaggio, c'era il blackout, pioveva fortissimo e lui ha fatto una scelta. A vent'anni bisogna accettarlo e aiutarlo a superarlo".

According to recent reports, come valuta la situazione a centrocampo, con Correia che sembra avere diversi compagni di reparto alternati al suo fianco? "Non credo sia colpa loro, è più colpa mia. Allenandoli tutti i giorni e avendone tanti in quel ruolo, scelgo di partita in partita quelli che, dal mio punto di vista, mi danno più garanzie. Leone è partito benissimo, poi ha avuto un momento in cui stava meno bene, ma adesso è di nuovo in ottima condizione, così come Piccinini ed Esteves. Siamo in tanti e devo fare delle scelte. Giocando con il doppio centrocampista, Correia sta giocando sempre e il suo compagno viene scelto in base al momento e a quello che vedo durante gli allenamenti. Parto sempre dal presupposto che posso anche sbagliare".

Infine, come stanno i difensori in vista della partita con l'Arezzo? "Anche in difesa ho diverse soluzioni e sfrutto i momenti dei singoli. In questo momento c'è chi sta dimostrando maggiore continuità di prestazioni. Caracciolo ha fatto due ottime partite: una giocando tutta la gara contro l'Empoli e un'altra entrando a freddo dopo venti minuti contro il Modena. Non era scontato e non era facile. Di partita in partita, anche in base agli avversari, scelgo la soluzione che ritengo migliore".
