Manchester City found guilty of 114 charges

📅 25 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2100 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester City have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought by the Premier League over breaches of its financial rules.
  • City face a range of sanctions from a fine to points deductions and even expulsion from the Premier League.
  • If the verdict is upheld, with City expected to appeal, it will also raise question marks over the 20 trophies the club have won under Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, whose Abu Dhabi group took over in 2008.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester City have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought by the Premier League over breaches of its financial rules. It is a decision that, if upheld, would equate to one of the biggest scandals in football history.

City face a range of sanctions from a fine to points deductions and even expulsion from the Premier League. Or a combination of all, under rule W51 of its handbook. No punishment has yet been announced.

If the verdict is upheld, with City expected to appeal, it will also raise question marks over the 20 trophies the club have won under Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, whose Abu Dhabi group took over in 2008.

The charges can be broken down into five categories and relate to a period from 2009-23 in which City won six League Cups, three FA Cups, seven league titles and the Champions League. There is the provision for removing past titles, but that would appear remote.

City have been the dominant force in English football for most of that time, but that status is under threat with a verdict that will send shockwaves around Europe and could have huge ramifications for the club.

That is unless they can win an appeal, with sources cautioning it still may take up to another two to three years for the case to be resolved, following on from an already five-year investigation.

The Premier League’s rules provide for an independent appeal board with broad powers, including the ability to uphold, vary or overturn the independent commission’s decision.

Recent findings suggest that it would therefore appear that despite the verdict, the case is far from being resolved and punishment decided. The details of the commission’s findings, when published, will be crucial to determining what happens next.

But if it is upheld, the verdict also opens up the possibility of City facing legal action from other clubs who feel they missed out on trophies and even merit money from league placings.

It is understood Premier League clubs are already discussing legal action and possible compensation claims as a result of the guilty verdict.

Each of those cases would have to be held individually, potentially leading to years more of litigation. Conversely, if City win their appeal, they too could take legal action against the Premier League the damage caused to their reputation.

It has been revealed that there has not yet been an official confirmation of the independent panel’s verdict from the Premier League. The Premier League declined to comment.

In a recent development, however, several sources have told Telegraph Sport that the panel has found City guilty of all but one of the charges they faced. The one that has not been proved is stated to be one of the most serious of the 115.

Sources indicate that the damning verdict for City is a major new test of fragile UK relations with the United Arab Emirates, with whom bilateral trade was worth £25bn last year. Redacted freedom of information documents, seen by Telegraph Sport, show Abu Dhabi hosted UK government officials including Lord Stockwood, then investment minister, as recently as February. Khaldoon Al Mubarak, the City chairman and trusted adviser to the UAE president, was present at the meeting. Government notes from the meeting recorded that he “noted they are very proud of what they have achieved through their investments in Manchester”.

According to recent reports, the Government previously caused acrimony among senior leaders in Abu Dhabi after putting forward legislation to ban foreign states from owning UK newspapers and news magazines. The intervention prompted the collapse of a takeover of The Telegraph in April 2024, which was largely funded by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the owner of City and vice-president and deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates.

Recent findings suggest that the previous UK government has admitted its embassy in Abu Dhabi and the Foreign Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) in London discussed the charges levelled at City by the Premier League. However it refused to disclose the correspondence.

City have steadfastly maintained they are innocent, promising “irrefutable” evidence in support of their position, and had assembled some of the most expensive lawyers in the country to argue their case. Despite the verdict, the club are understood to be confident that it will win the argument in the end. Senior figures are said to be calm about the latest development, as significant as it seems.

City rebuilt their team this summer and it is understood that signings were brought in on conventional player contracts, rather than terms including clauses triggered in the event of a heavy punishment. Given the club have consistently denied breaching financial regulations, and their deals for fresh players to work with head coach Enzo Maresca underlines their position.

According to recent reports, on Friday, a City spokesman remarked: “The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such, Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the club’s statement of February 2023.

“The club have diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.”.

Sources close to Pep Guardiola, the former City manager who stepped down last summer after 10 years of remarkable success at the club, including a treble triumph in 2023 and an unprecedented fourth straight league title in 2024, insist he has not been informed of any verdict.

In the days after City were first charged, Guardiola mounted a fierce defence of the club, claiming: “I am fully convinced we will be [proved] innocent.”.

The verdict vindicates the Premier League’s decision to launch an investigation after explosive allegations that City had routinely broken financial rules were first made in Der Spiegel in 2018 based on the Football Leaks documents.

Uefa previously accused City of breaches of its financial regulations and revealed in 2020 that it was suspending the club from the Champions League for two years for “overstating” sponsorship revenue between 2012 and 2016.

Industry observers note that city denied the Uefa charges and, after an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport, the two-year ban was overturned. Cas found that a number of the claims brought by Uefa had fallen outside a five-year “time bar” and others were “not established”.

It did, however, still impose a €10m fine after ruling that City failed to cooperate with investigators. City had previously also agreed a settlement with Uefa of €20m in 2014 following an investigation into their finances.

Industry observers note that legal experts agreed that the commission’s verdict is far from the end of the case. Yasin Patel, barrister at Church Court Chambers, mentioned: “City’s lawyers will now analyse this decision and look at the options open to them to appeal, which may include procedural impropriety, wrongful interpretation of law, and legal errors – importantly, they can guarantee an appeal.

It has been revealed that “Sanctions could include a major fine, points deduction, relegation or even all three. Factoring in whether titles and trophies should be stripped, whether other clubs have been robbed of further revenue and opportunities due to City’s wrongdoings and losses incurred, we safely say that this is only the first chapter of a long-running legal saga that will not end any time soon.”.

In a recent development, ian Hargreaves, partner with specialist disputes firm Quillon Law, said the verdict was “not the end of the story but the beginning of a new phase”, and added: “There is also the question of whether the panel’s decision can withstand a hard-fought appeal, and on what grounds any challenge might be brought. Much will depend on the detail of the panel’s findings and reasoning, which will inevitably be closely scrutinised by both sides.”.

Former Manchester City midfielder Rodri, who won the Ballon d’Or during his trophy-laden spell at the club, said he believed the club were innocent.

“For the players, it’s different than it is for journalists. I can understand all opinions, but we try to stay positive,” the Spain midfielder said while on international duty.

“When you see all the people who worked hard at City to achieve success, you know what we achieved can’t be taken away. It wasn’t paid for with money, but with effort and teamwork. Everything we achieved was deserved; we marked one of the great eras of English football. I believe in the club’s innocence – we already went through this in 2020.”.

Andy Burnham, the Prime Minister, said: “I think we would all need to study the independent commission’s report in some considerable detail before reaching any conclusions.”.

Zohran Kwame Mamdani, the mayor of New York, posted “114” in relation to the charges while former Manchester United players David de Gea and Rio Ferdinand both asked whether they should be due winner’s medals from past seasons.

The Premier League statement in February 2023 noted that “a number of alleged breaches” had been referred to an independent commission. It then detailed each specific rule against each season in which the alleged breach took place. The precise number was not clear from the statement and led to varying reports between 115 and 130. Friday’s news suggested the figure was 115.

Recent findings suggest that all the way to 2009-10, the first full season following the club’s takeover by Sheikh Mansour, who is a member of the Abu Dhabi Royal family and the vice president of the United Arab Emirates. There were charges relating to all 14 seasons until the Premier League completed their investigation during the 2022-23 campaign. In that time, City won seven Premier League titles, six League Cups, three FA Cups and the Champions League. They have since won another league title – the first club to do so four times in a row – as well as the Uefa Super Cup, the Fifa Club World Cup and the FA Cup and League Cup double last season.

Industry observers note that they can be split into five groups. The biggest relates to the seasons from 2009-10 until 2017-18 and the requirement for clubs to provide accurate financial information and act in the utmost good faith.

The next set of rules concern the full disclosure of manager and player payments. The alleged manager breaches related to the period between 2009-10 and 2012-13, when Roberto Mancini was leading the team. The alleged breaches with respect to player payments relate to all of the seasons between 2010-11 and 2015-16.

Recent findings suggest that as well as providing financial detail, clubs were required to meet Uefa and Premier League rules which were designed to bring a club’s spending broadly in line with their income by placing set limits on losses. City were charged with breaches of Uefa’s licencing and financial fair play rules from 2013-14 until 2017-18, and the Premier League’s profit and sustainability rules from 2015-16 until 2017-18.

The final set of charges spanned the five seasons during which City were being investigated by the Premier League and rules that require members to cooperate in the utmost good faith by providing information and documents.

According to recent reports, A full picture will only emerge when the commission publishes its findings but we know that the Premier League investigation began in December 2018 following allegations in the German newspaper Der Spiegel based on the Football Leaks documents. These included alleged payments to former manager Mancini for consultancy work at an Abu Dhabi-based club that was separate to his regular contract at City.

We also know that City were alleged to have breached rules over setting out image rights payments to players in their club contract. Der Spiegel reported that the Premier League investigation also focused on payments to under-age players, as well as whether club sponsors were paying for commercial deals themselves or a significant proportion was in fact effectively coming from owner Sheikh Mansour.

Sources indicate that city have always denied breaking any rules. In response to the Premier League statement about the alleged breaches, they stated that they have “irrefutable evidence” to support their position and “look forward to this matter being put to rest once and for all.”.

At the start of the hearing in September 2024, Guardiola also noted: “Wait for the independent panel. We believe we have not done anything wrong.”.

In a recent development, of the Football Leaks documents, City stated: “We will not be providing any comment on out-of-context materials. The attempt to damage the club’s reputation is organised and clear.”.

#154206. Monza, Juric: "Dobbiamo andare oltre i nostri limiti per mettere in difficoltà la Roma"

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1584 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Tuttomercatoweb ↗ Open Full Page

Monza, Juric: "Dobbiamo andare oltre i nostri limiti per mettere in difficoltà la Roma"

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1584 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tuttomercatoweb

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ivan Juric, tecnico del Monza, ha parlato in conferenza stampa in vista della sfida di domenica con la Roma.
  • According to recent reports, mister, dopo la vittoria sulla Fiorentina avrebbe preferito evitare una Roma in grande forma, allenata tra l'altro dal suo maestro e amico Gasperini?
  • According to recent reports, "Non mi dispiace, perché prima o poi devi affrontare tutti.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ivan Juric, tecnico del Monza, ha parlato in conferenza stampa in vista della sfida di domenica con la Roma.

According to recent reports, mister, dopo la vittoria sulla Fiorentina avrebbe preferito evitare una Roma in grande forma, allenata tra l'altro dal suo maestro e amico Gasperini? Inoltre, molti suoi colleghi sostengono che seguire la partita dalla tribuna, quando si è squalificati, permetta di cogliere meglio alcuni aspetti tattici. È d'accordo?

According to recent reports, "Non mi dispiace, perché prima o poi devi affrontare tutti. Non penso mai a evitare qualcuno: li affronti e basta. Per quanto riguarda la seconda domanda, è vero, spesso anche durante gli allenamenti ci mettiamo in alto per osservare meglio le situazioni. Dalla tribuna si vedono alcune cose in maniera più chiara, come è successo anche l'altro giorno, mentre altre si notano meno: i piccoli particolari, le espressioni dei giocatori, alcuni aspetti che dalla panchina riesci a cogliere meglio. A livello tattico, però, dall'alto si vede sicuramente di più. Ricordo, per esempio, una partita dell'Atalanta contro il Paris Saint-Germain, quando un allenatore aveva seguito il primo tempo dalla tribuna ed era poi sceso per apportare le modifiche necessarie.".

In a recent development, tornando alla partita con la Fiorentina, cosa ha visto meglio dalla tribuna rispetto alla panchina? Dal punto di vista tattico, il centrocampo a cinque, anche con il rientro di capitan Pessina, è attualmente l'assetto che garantisce maggiore equilibrio e pericolosità?

In a recent development, "All'inizio la partita non mi era sembrata positiva, perché non eravamo aggressivi come avrei voluto. Dal 25' abbiamo iniziato a recuperare più palloni, a spingere e a prenderci qualche rischio in più. Abbiamo preso in mano la partita e, nei venti minuti finali del primo tempo e nei primi quindici della ripresa, abbiamo fatto quello che chiedevo: abbiamo segnato, creato un'altra occasione con Brindelli e una con Pessina, dominando la gara. Magari abbiamo concesso qualcosa in contropiede, ma era proprio quello che volevo vedere. Successivamente ci siamo abbassati per gestire il risultato.

Per quanto riguarda l'assetto tattico, le richieste che faccio ad Akinsanmiro sono le stesse che facevo a Ngonge e Colpani. Cambia però l'interpretazione del ruolo: Akinsanmiro può darci qualcosa in più in determinate situazioni, nei raddoppi e nella compattezza. Devo dire, comunque, che anche Ngonge e Colpani hanno svolto un buon lavoro difensivo. In fase offensiva, invece, magari ci manca qualcosa rispetto alle loro caratteristiche. Akinsanmiro è molto bravo negli inserimenti, riesce a portare via altri giocatori e a liberare spazi per i compagni. È sicuramente un'opzione valida.".

Qual è l'aspetto che teme maggiormente della Roma? E secondo lei la squadra di Gasperini è una delle candidate allo scudetto?

"Basta guardare i risultati: segnano quattro o cinque gol a partita. Ogni squadra che va all'Olimpico rischia davvero tanto, ma anche in trasferta stanno attraversando un momento straordinario. Hanno gioco e qualità. Gasperini è riuscito a trasmettere alla squadra tutto quello che aveva in mente e probabilmente continuerà a farlo. Adesso si vede che vanno forte: sono una squadra difficilissima da affrontare.

Per quanto riguarda lo scudetto, la considero una delle principali candidate insieme all'Inter. Vedremo se anche la Lazio riuscirà a mantenere questo ritmo, ma la Roma sta andando davvero forte. In questo momento mi sembra quella più difficile da affrontare, con più soluzioni offensive e un gioco che rende complicato capire da dove possa arrivare il pericolo.".

In a recent development, poco più di un mese fa avete affrontato la Roma all'Olimpico, giocando molto bene soprattutto nel secondo tempo e mostrando grande coraggio anche in inferiorità numerica. Domenica potrebbero servirvi lo stesso atteggiamento e una maggiore attenzione?

"Ho notato che le squadre che provano soltanto a chiudersi e a gestire gli spazi, senza aggredire la Roma, fanno molta fatica e finiscono per subire anche cinque gol. Chi invece prova ad aggredirla riesce a metterla in difficoltà, anche se deve riuscire a mantenere quell'intensità per tutta la partita. Finché ci riesce, può creare problemi alla Roma. Noi faremo la nostra partita, seguendo le nostre idee e cercando di andare oltre i nostri limiti per metterli in difficoltà.".

In a recent development, domenica tornerà all'Olimpico da avversario della Roma, dopo la difficile esperienza sulla panchina giallorossa. Che accoglienza si aspetta? E da quell'esperienza si è portato via qualche insegnamento umano o professionale che oggi le torna utile a Monza?

Sources indicate that "Penso che siano soprattutto le esperienze negative a insegnarti di più. Anche quelle che ho vissuto io sono state molto utili, anche se emotivamente non è stato facile affrontarle. Sono proprio le esperienze negative che ti fanno crescere maggiormente. Quelle belle ed entusiasmanti le ricordi con piacere, ma credo che dalle difficoltà si impari di più. In ogni caso, la vita va avanti: raccogli quello che hai imparato e guardi al futuro. Adesso c'è il Monza, il mio obiettivo è capire come deve giocare questa squadra e come far crescere i ragazzi. Ho soltanto questo in testa.".

In a recent development, nelle ultime partite abbiamo visto il passaggio a un centrocampo più solido, con cinque centrocampisti. La fase difensiva è nettamente migliorata?

According to recent reports, "Per me no, assolutamente. Voi vi basate sui gol subiti, ma non considerate i tiri, le occasioni e quello che succede in campo. Non sono d'accordo. La partita contro l'Atalanta, per esempio, è stata imparagonabile rispetto a quella contro la Fiorentina: abbiamo fatto molto meglio contro l'Atalanta, anche se abbiamo perso. Nel primo tempo contro di loro abbiamo concesso zero occasioni. È diverso. Secondo me si guarda soltanto ed esclusivamente al risultato.".

In un certo senso possiamo dire che anche il Monza ha i suoi Dybala e Malen, in Varela e Robinson. Da qui a gennaio sarà importante recuperare e riabilitare, anche dal punto di vista mentale, giocatori che oggi sono diventati seconde linee, come Cutrone e Colpani?

It has been revealed that "Io aggiungerei anche Ngonge e Zeballos, oltre naturalmente a Cutrone e Colpani. Il calcio è fatto così: quando giochi una volta a settimana hai due ragazzi che stanno facendo davvero bene. In questo momento inserirei anche Motta, che ogni volta che entra mi dà grandi soddisfazioni per il modo in cui interpreta la partita, per l'entusiasmo e per quel sorriso che porta in campo.

È chiaro quello che dici, ma anche l'altra sera, nella partita del Paris Saint-Germain, abbiamo visto un esempio clamoroso: al 60' sono entrati Dybala e Malen. Nel calcio di oggi, con questi ritmi e questa intensità, avere tanti giocatori di qualità diventa fondamentale. Spero davvero che questi ragazzi non si sentano sottovalutati, ma che continuino a lavorare forte e possano darci una grande mano durante le partite.".

Il clean sheet contro la Fiorentina ha dato morale al reparto difensivo. In particolare, Andrea Carboni ha disputato una grande prestazione. Come valuta la sua partita? Ci sono novità sugli infortunati e come mai Ciurria non è stato convocato nell'ultima gara?

Sources indicate that "Sono molto contento per Carboni, perché penso che abbia disputato una bellissima partita. Non so se sia stata la sua migliore prestazione, ma è stato sempre molto concentrato. È un ragazzo con una mentalità pazzesca. Ha riposato per due o tre settimane e anche questo, a volte, serve per recuperare energie. Ha fatto davvero una bella prestazione.

According to recent reports, per quanto riguarda Ciurria, in questo momento siamo in 27 e devo fare delle scelte, non soltanto per le partite ma anche durante gli allenamenti. È una situazione complicata: quando organizzi le partitelle dieci contro dieci, devi lasciare fuori quattro o cinque giocatori. Spero che questa situazione si risolva a gennaio, perché è dannosa e non mi piace per niente.

It has been revealed that purtroppo, dopo l'infortunio, Ciurria è rimasto fuori dalle rotazioni. È un momento particolare per lui e mi dispiace. Per quanto riguarda gli infortuni, Akinsanmiro ha preso una brutta botta all'inizio e ha avuto bisogno anche di alcuni punti di sutura. Ieri non è riuscito ad allenarsi, oggi ha fatto qualcosa e spero di averlo a disposizione. Per il resto, dalla prossima settimana dovrebbero esserci tutti.".

Sources indicate that il recupero di Ziolkowski permetterà alla difesa di fare un ulteriore salto di qualità? Come procede invece la competizione tra i due portieri, Tornqvist e Thiam?

In a recent development, "Ziolkowski è un giocatore di grandissimo potenziale e ha ampi margini di miglioramento sotto diversi aspetti, come del resto tutti i nostri giocatori, a eccezione di qualche elemento più esperto. È già diventato un giocatore che può scendere in campo, entrare e darci una mano. Siamo contenti di lui e ha le caratteristiche giuste per essere importante per la squadra.

Industry observers note that per quanto riguarda Thiam e Tornqvist, come per tutti i nostri giocatori, vedo aspetti positivi e altri negativi. Per giocare devono essere al cento per cento, sia mentalmente sia fisicamente. Penso che Thiam abbia fatto due settimane ottime. Quando è rimasto qui avevo bisogno di un portiere bravo nelle uscite in determinate situazioni, perché immaginavo che nel finale potessero arrivare diversi cross verso Pellegrino e Beto. Ha lavorato molto bene e ci ha dato anche la possibilità di ripartire.

It has been revealed that per il momento non ho stabilito una gerarchia precisa: a volte giocherà uno, a volte l'altro. Abbiamo cambiato anche il modo di difendere sui calci piazzati, passando alla marcatura a uomo, che non avevo mai utilizzato prima. Finora è andata bene. Proviamo soluzioni e varianti diverse perché voglio che tutti siano motivati e concentrati, senza sapere in anticipo quello che succederà.".

It has been revealed that beppe Bergomi, opinionista, si è così espresso a SkySport commentando la vittoria del Milan contro l'Olympiacos ad Atene: "Ci sono certi giocatori che magari vanno a giocare tra le linee e si trovano meglio perché lì magari devi avere un certo tipo di abilità tecnica, invece altri che se li porti proprio con la riga laterale vicina nell'uno contro uno ti saltano. Hutchinson rientra, mette, crossa e allora può determinare maggiormente. Quella è stata la mossa decisiva. In più io continuo a pensare che nel primo tempo, quando Rabiot gioca in quella posizione, poi lui la svuota per andare ad aprirsi a sinistra e lì rimane un vuoto. Invece quando tu lo riempi con gli Jashari, il solito Modrić e Musah, lui può avere più libertà e ha meno compiti di copertura che poi dà. Quindi alla fine: il Milan si è sistemato meglio sul campo, le responsabilità, i cambi, ha inciso tutto quanto e continuo a pensare che è una squadra in crescita".

Scotland’s ramped-up second-half performance offered some cause for optimism as Sébastien Pocognoli’s tenure as head coach began with a goalless draw with Slovenia in Ljubljana.

The 39-year-old Belgian head coach, appointed in August as Steve Clarke’s successor, refreshed the side for the Nations League Group B1 opener in the Stozice Stadium, but they were fortunate on a couple of occasions at least not to fall behind before rallying before the break.

Scotland had been insipid and uninspiring for most of the first half but after the interval they played with pace and purpose as Slovenia captain and goalkeeper Jan Oblak became a key figure, making saves from Oli McBurnie and Kieron Bowie.

Oli McBurnie spurns a chance for Scotland.It remains goalless between Slovenia and Scotland.📺 Watch on BBC One pic.twitter.com/sldzhNCGGb.

“It took us a bit of getting used to in the first half, the way the gaffer wants to play,” McBurnie told BBC Scotland.

It has been revealed that “We created enough chances to win the game. I should have scored. I was asked to play a different position and I enjoyed it. I’d rather be getting in the positions than not getting chances.

“Second half was a lot more of what the manager wanted from us. It was waves of pressure and the only thing missing was a goal or two.”.

However, the goal that would have made the former Union Saint-Gilloise and Monaco manager’s debut as an international boss more memorable ultimately failed to arrive.

In this extended international break, the Scots will host Switzerland at Hampden on Tuesday and then travel to North Macedonia before taking on Slovenia in Glasgow, with the Tartan Army hoping to see further improvement – and goals.

September 29: Scotland vs Switzerland.

October 3: North Macedonia vs Scotland.

October 6: Scotland vs Slovenia.

November 13: Scotland vs North Macedonia.

November 16: Switzerland vs Scotland.

Speaking to BBC Scotland, the debutant remarked: “Thought we struggled to get into the game first half, but second half we completely dominated the game.

In a recent development, “They’ve got a top goalie who made really good saves. So many positives to take and a clean sheet as well.

“We changed shape a wee bit at half-time to get more control and that did really well for us.

“It’s a massive game again on Tuesday so it’s notable to recover now and go again.

“I’ve played on the left-hand side for a couple of years now, so I’m comfortable doing that.

According to recent reports, “We’ve had a great week. A upcoming manager, new way of playing and new faces in camp. It’s just the chances we need to take - the fact we’re creating the chances stands us in good stead.”.

The striker told BBC Scotland: “It took us a bit of getting used to in the first half, the way the gaffer wants to play.

In a recent development, “Second half was a lot more of what the manager wanted from us. It was waves of pressure and the only thing missing was a goal or two.”.

According to recent reports, pocognoli’s first game in charge of Scotland ends in a goalless draw. The visitors produced a dominant second-half display, but their final ball and end-product was severely lacking in crucial moments. Ure, Hickey, Gilmour, McBurnie and Bowie all came close to scoring, but no one could break the deadlock.

Scotland cannot find a way past the impenetrable Oblak. There will be just two minutes of added time for the visitors to possibly score a late winner.

Karnicnik catches Robertson with a late lunging tackle and receives a yellow card, giving Scotland a chance to get the ball into the box.

The hosts make their fifth alteration of the afternoon, with Cerin withdrawn and Lovric on instead.

How has Bowie missed?! Gilmour finds Bowie with an outstanding pass through the centre of Slovenia’s defence. The substitute takes a touch then scuffs a rushed finish wide. Bowie has to do better there!

However, Pocognoli’s squad have only been together for a few days and are playing in a new system. Can they produce a more inspired second-half performance?

Despite Scotland’s late push for an opening goal at the end of the first half, the two sides head in level at the break. Slovenia started on the front-foot, with Sporar and Drkusic both going close for the hosts, before Ure struck the post to be denied a dream debut goal.

A new-look attack is spearheaded by the returning Oli McBurnie and 22-year-old Robbie Ure, who like Welsh, will also make his Scotland debut.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this UEFA Nations League B, Group 1 match as Slovenia host Scotland at Stozice Stadium in Ljubljana.

It has been revealed that scotland qualified for their first World Cup in 28 years this summer, but they exited the tournament with a whimper after failing to finish as one of the best third-place group sides. Steve Clarke’s men beat tournament debutants Haiti 1-0 in their opening match, before falling to defeats without scoring against Morocco and Brazil.

Following the World Cup, Clarke stepped down as Scotland’s head coach, ending a seven-year tenure, and was replaced by Belgian manager Sebastien Pocognoli. The former Monaco boss will take charge of his first game in his latest role today and will be itching to make an encouraging start in a new era for Scottish football.

Over this extended international break, Pocognoli’s side will also face Switzerland and North Macedonia, as well as a return fixture against Slovenia in Scotland on October 6 to round off a busy period.

While Scotland took part in the World Cup, Slovenia were reflecting on their hugely disappointing qualification performance, where they finished third in their group behind Switzerland and Kosovo without winning and netting just three goals across six matches.

Manchester United striker Benjamin Sesko – Slovenia’s star man and most well-known player – withdrew from Bostjan Cesar’s squad earlier this week after the recurrence of a shin injury caused the 23-year-old to completely miss the 1-1 draw against Fulham last Sunday.

Scotland have a few notable absences, with Scott McTominay, Che Adams and Lawrence Shankland all unavailable, but Billy Gilmour returns to the fold after missing the World Cup through injury, Oli McBurnie has been recalled and Sevilla striker Robbie Ure has received his first senior call-up.

Kick-off is at 14:00, with team news coming shortly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 21:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 12:27 EST, 24 November 2026.

Despite being shipped off to Germany’s finest finishing school for young English talent, Ethan Nwaneri’s time at Borussia Dortmund is already at a crossroads.

The 19-year-old joined the Bundesliga side on a season-long loan in September after enduring a frustrating five-month spell at Marseille earlier in the year.

This was supposed to be the loan move to reinvigorate one of England’s best young forwards, at a club well-versed in doing exactly that.

Nwaneri became the fifth Englishman aged 21 or under to sign for Dortmund in the past decade, following in the footsteps of Jadon Sancho, Jude and Jobe Bellingham, and Jamie Gittens. The stars seemed aligned for Nwaneri to shine.

But the opposite has happened. Having impressed and forced a Hoffenheim own goal off the bench on his Dortmund debut, Nwaneri started the team’s next four Bundesliga matches, but was hooked off around the hour mark in each one. The teenager has not made a starting XI since a goalless draw with Union Berlin on October 17.

It is understood Arsenal – who host Dortmund in the Champions League tonight – are closely monitoring the situation around Nwaneri’s lack of minutes, and there is a January recall clause in his contract. The clause was initially inserted as insurance in case an attacking injury crisis arose at Arsenal. Nwaneri's lack of minutes wasn't expected.

Ethan Nwaneri is on loan at Borussia Dortmund from Arsenal but has struggled for minutes – he last started a match on October 17.

The 19-year-old is one of the most talented youngsters to emerge from Arsenal's prolific Hale End academy, but his career is in danger of stalling on loan in Germany.

So why isn’t his move at Dortmund, a club that made their name by developing young players, working out?

Well, Nwaneri's short career so far has been a complicated one, featuring enormous highs and challenging hurdles. To understand his trajectory, you have to look back at his time at Hale End.

Having risen through the academy rapidly upon joining aged eight, Nwaneri burst onto the first-team scene in September 2022 against Brentford, becoming the youngest player to appear in the Premier League, aged 15 years and 181 days.

Mikel Arteta still values the player but hinted on Monday that he needs to produce more than just ‘moments’.

‘You can have patches, but to find that consistency and to play a major amount of minutes and have a huge impact in big football clubs like Arsenal or Dortmund, it's extremely difficult,’ he said.

‘That's the reality. You can just shine in moments, but moments are not enough. Now you need to show the consistency. Ethan has the capacity and the mentality to do that, and it takes some time.’.

Sources indicate that there's a feeling at Arsenal that Nwaneri has time on his side and shouldn’t be written off. He signed a five-year deal in August 2025 after all, with a blueprint to fully integrate the attacker into the first-team squad. His brother Emerson, 16, is thriving with the Under 18s.

However, if Nwaneri were to be sold in future, he would, as an academy graduate, generate pure profit on Arsenal's accounts.

‘His time at Borussia has been a disappointment so far because he was brought in to help immediately after Giannis Konstantelias tore his ACL,’ claims Sebastian Wessling, who has covered Dortmund for 15 years at the Funke Media Group.

According to recent reports, ‘They tried to bring Nwaneri in, the summer before. So having tracked and spoken to him previously, they thought he would be ideal for short-term help. But he really hasn’t been that, it’s not worked out well so far.

‘He’s found it difficult to contribute with goals, assists, or just generally in Dortmund’s offensive game.

Recent findings suggest that ‘What the coach is looking for is a player to make a lot of runs in behind. Whereas Nwaneri looks to drop deep and have time on the ball, which the manager, Niko Kovac, isn’t looking for.’.

'He lacks confidence and I think that shows in his play,' says Dortmund expert Sebastian Wessling of Nwaneri.

There is still a serious player in Nwaneri, as seen in his two assists for England Under 21s in their 3-2 victory over France last week.

According to recent reports, nwaneri's lack of confidence and progress feel striking. This summer, he joined England's pre-World Cup training camp in Florida, and was an unused substitute in the warm-up match against Newly introduced Zealand. Nwaneri was alongside Bournemouth's Alex Scott, Fulham's Josh King and Liverpool's Rio Ngumoha – both Scott and Ngumoha have since made their senior England debuts, while King made Thomas Tuchel's squad this month. All three are flourishing as Nwaneri struggles to even feature.

To make matters worse for him, back at Arsenal 16-year-old Max Dowman is competing for a place in the starting XI. Nwaneri may have bundles of talent, but he is yet to fully kick on.

Wessling adds: ‘He lacks confidence and I think that shows in his play. Niko wants him to be brave on the pitch, but he plays it very safe.

Sources indicate that ‘When he did feature, he often played short passes and didn’t advance Dortmund’s play. He’s not a total disappointment, but he hasn’t really contributed.’.

There is still a serious player in Nwaneri, as seen in his two assists for England Under 21s in their 3-2 victory over France last week. He is eligible to feature at the Emirates tonight, and will be desperate to show Arsenal what they are missing.

Industry observers note that in any case, his next two months at Dortmund will reveal plenty about his future. It’s now about consistency – more than mere ‘moments’.

Cesena, Diamanti avvisa: "Se pensiamo di essere forti, è un problema"

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that due vittorie consecutive contro Hellas Verona e Ascoli, entusiasmo crescente e una squadra che sembra aver trovato la propria identità. Ma Alessandro Diamanti non vuole cali di tensione. Alla vigilia della trasferta contro il Vicenza, valida per la 14ª giornata di Serie B, il tecnico del Cesena ha richiamato i suoi alla massima attenzione, mettendo in guardia dal rischio di sentirsi arrivati dopo gli ultimi risultati.

"Se qualcuno pensa che siamo diventati forti - riporta MondoCesena -, sarà un grandissimo problema. Comunque non vedo giocatori che in questi due giorni abbiano cambiato atteggiamento, anche perché non lo permetterei e non c’è nessun motivo di farlo".

Industry observers note that il messaggio è chiaro: "Vincere le partite deve essere solo una cosa che ti aiuta a credere nelle cose che fai, a lavorare più duramente e più intensamente, a crederci di più e a curare meglio il dettaglio. Le vittorie aiutano a questo, non a rilassarsi".

Industry observers note that sul fronte opposto ci sarà un Vicenza che ha appena cambiato guida tecnica, affidando la panchina a Davide Dionigi dopo l'esonero di Fabio Gallo. Un'incognita che Diamanti non sottovaluta: "È normale che la tensione debba essere duplicata, perché sicuramente quando si cambia allenatore c’è una reazione aggressiva, dura, cattiva. Bisogna aspettarsela, sappiamo che succederà".

Capitolo formazione: il Cesena dovrà fare a meno di Bisoli e Bohinen, mentre resta da valutare Frabotta. Possibile invece il ritorno tra le opzioni di Schirone, che sta lavorando con il gruppo da una decina di giorni: "Sta sempre meglio: certo che sarà un'opzione".

Diamanti non teme particolarmente le possibili variazioni tattiche legate al cambio in panchina del Vicenza: "Non è mai un salto nel buio. Abbiamo già giocato contro la difesa a quattro, contro quella a tre, contro tutti i moduli: bisogna essere bravi a capire 5, 10, 12 minuti prima o durante la gara quello che proveranno a fare".

It has been revealed that infine, il tecnico bianconero ha voluto sottolineare l'importanza dell'atteggiamento rispetto alle questioni puramente tattiche: "Non c’è tattica senza energia, senza entusiasmo, senza combattere". Il percorso del Cesena passa proprio da qui: continuare a crescere, senza lasciarsi condizionare dai giudizi esterni e mantenendo quell'identità che Diamanti vuole costruire giorno dopo giorno.
